articleTitle: Design of Lightweight Custom IP Core on FPGA to Discriminate Brain Tumors of MR Data
abstract: In response to growing demand for efficient medical image processing methods on FPGA, this work presents the design of a custom IP core for brain tumor classification using morphological features. This IP core uses the ZYNQ 7000 Processing System on PYNQ Z2 platform. The present work focuses on minimization of classifier’s t raining complexity by extracting 17 significant morphological features from tumor data. The tumors are then categorised with the best accuracy of 90% using a linear Support Vector Machine (SVM). As this streamlined methodology employs hand-crafted features to simplify the classification model, the proposed IP core uses only 1.92% of FPGA resources and 21 mW of power. The current work presents a potential design for scalable and hardware-accelerated medical imaging systems attaining minimal power with high efficiency.

articleTitle: Q-learning based Droplet Routing in Digital Microfluidic Biochip
abstract: Digital microfluidic biochip (DMFB) is popular as laboratory on chip device. Droplet routing in DMFB is a major research area under computer aided design. Major goal of this CAD based research is to efficiently manage droplet movement on DMFB to complete the task in less time using a smaller number of unique electrodes. Application of machine learning methods in this domain is very less as traditional supervised learning mechanisms are not suitable due to lack of proper labelled training data. This article proposes a Q-learning based approach to accomplish the goal of droplet routing. DMFB board serves as environment, droplets as agent and their rewards are based on target directed movement and fluidic constraints. Initial routing trace records an accumulated rewards which later helps in identifying the right paths with optimal solution. Experimental analysis shows some encouraging results in terms of routing completion time and total unique electrode usage over the existing research reports.

articleTitle: Investigation of Stack Oxide Double Gate Junction Less Transistor for Ammonia Gas Sensing
abstract: In the today's world, ammonia gas has many wider applications and can be used in the manufacturing of textiles, chemical fertilizers, plastics, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, food and beverages etc. when the leakage of ammonia gas happens leads to severe health issues in humans so there is a need of the hour to design efficient ammonia gas sensor. In this paper a detailed 2D model of SO-DGJLT transistor is developed by using COMSOL Multiphysics. By using this model parameters like I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf>/V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GS</inf>, Subthreshold slope, threshold voltage, Sensitivity, Selectivity, can be calculated the change in electrical characteristics and a new device is comparable with previously designed gas sensor Junction less vertical TFET (JL-VTFET) to check the performance of the device Stack oxide double gate junction less transistor. Ammonia gas sensor with high performance is developed for the future outlook.

articleTitle: Avalanche Photodetector for Telecommunication Wavelengths
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive simulation study of an avalanche photodetector (APD) operating at wavelengths 1310 nm and 1550 nm, utilizing Lumerical’s FDTD and Charge solvers. Key performance metrics, including dark current, photocurrent, responsivity and multiplication gain were analyzed as functions of reverse bias voltage. The results indicate that the APD exhibits a lower dark current at 1550 nm, achieving higher photocurrent and responsivity at 1310 nm. Notably, the multiplication gain remains consistent across both the wavelengths, suggesting that the avalanche multiplication process is predominantly influenced by the applied bias and material properties rather than the incident wavelength. These findings provide valuable insights for optimizing the APD performance in optical communication systems operating within these wavelength regimes.

articleTitle: High-Performance ASIC Design for Pipelined DDR2 SDRAM Controllers
abstract: The embedded system must be able to run multiple apps simultaneously. The popularity of Double Data Rate Synchronous Dynamic Random Access Memory (DDR2 SDRAM) is attributed to its speed and burst access capabilities. An interface-like SDRAM module that helps to decrease power consumption and increase frequency is DDR2 SDRAM. DDR transferring is supported by synchronous dynamic random-access memory. There are several operations that need to be pipelined in the memory controller. Both rising and falling edges of the clock signal are used to send data twice a cycle. An optimized DDR2 SDRAM controller with reduced leakage power and area is presented in this paper, enhancing the efficiency of VLSI applications. In comparison to existing models, this design reduces area by 64.2%, leakage power by 17.7%, and dynamic power by 9.8%. With 2,978ps latency and 6,978 ps timing slack, the proposed controller ensures high-speed, energy-efficient performance.

articleTitle: Advanced Spatial-Temporal Framework for Deforestation Monitoring with CNN-LSTM Hybrid Architecture
abstract: Deforestation poses significant threats to environmental sustainability and reliable and real time monitoring solutions are needed. We propose a hybrid framework for detecting deforestation using camera trap imagery that combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. Extracting spatial features through the CNN layers and temporal sequences performed through the LSTM layers, ensures a greater classification. To deal with class imbalance and generalize, the methodology uses ensemble techniques and data augmentation. We obtained superior performance for the proposed model compared to traditional methods (Random Forest and SVM) with an accuracy of 94%, precision of 92%, recall of 93% and an AUC-ROC of 96%. The Grad-CAM visual explanations revealed regions that affect model decision, providing insights into the interpretability of the model. Although there are limitations such as environmental biases and occasionally misclassifications, the proposed model is a scalable and efficient solution for real time deforestation detection. The results obtained are relevant to the development of advanced monitoring systems that support global conservation efforts and sustainable forest management.

articleTitle: Deriving ECG Features from PPG Signals Using Machine Learning Approaches
abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG) plays a crucial role in diagnosing cardiovascular diseases, while Photoplethysmography (PPG) offers a non-invasive alternative for continuous heart monitoring, especially in wearable technology. Leveraging PPG for ECG feature estimation can enhance early detection and proactive management of heart-related conditions. This study presents a cost-effective approach to estimating key ECG parameters by utilizing the time-domain characteristics of PPG. Statistical analysis was conducted to identify the most relevant PPG features for ECG estimation, which were then used to develop a predictive model using artificial neural networks, linear regression, and random forest algorithms. Experimental results on a benchmark dataset confirm that the proposed methodology achieves high accuracy in ECG parameter estimation. The proposed cost-effective device (approx. one thousand), integrating feature selection, ensures high classification accuracy, real-time monitoring, and timely alerts, enhancing practical usability.

articleTitle: Performance enhancement of surface plasmon resonance-based sensor through platinum diselenide for glucose sensing
abstract: Refractive index-based sensors provide high sensitivity and more accuracy for a wide range of analytes across various applications like biomedical diagnostics, environmental monitoring, and chemical analysis. This work proposes a surface plasmon resonance (SPR) based refractive index sensor using a Kretschmann configuration under an angle interrogation scheme. A bi-metallic layer of aluminum and gold is used as a plasmonic metal over a coupling prism. Two distinct 2D nanomaterials, platinum diselenide and molybdenum disulfide, are stacked with an optimized thickness on top of these metals to enhance the performance. The transfer matrix and finite element methods are used to calculate reflection characteristics under a TM polarized light of wavelength 1550nm. A high value of Figure of merit 767 RIU⁻¹ with a sensitivity of 176.5°/RIU is observed while sensing glucose concentrations in urine samples. The proposed sensor has the potential for sensing applications across different fields where any phenomenon on the surface leads to refractive index modifications.

articleTitle: Total Ionizing Dose (TID) Analysis of FinFET-Based CMOS NAND and NOR Logic Gates
abstract: The total ionizing dose analysis of CMOS-based NAND and NOR logic gate is presented. In the normal operating conditions, universal logic gates function as expected. However, exposure to radiation distorts the output of both NAND and NOR gates. In particular, the NOR gate experiences significant degradation due to the parallel connection of n-FinFETs, which increases the overall trap charge density in the circuit. The accumulation of these trap charges at the gate oxide interface further deteriorates the post-radiation output, impacting the reliability of the circuit in radiation-prone environments.

articleTitle: Comparative Performance Analysis of Silicon on Insulator Vertical Super Thin Body FETs Using Silicon and Germanium Body
abstract: This article investigates the comparative performance of a Silicon on Insulator vertical super-thin body (SOI VSTB) FET using silicon and germanium materials, utilizing the 3D Senaturus TCAD tool. The impact of stress on the transfer characteristics for Si/Ge VSTB FET is analyzed. In high-performance circuits, germanium demonstrates superior performance, increasing on-state current (ION) significantly, while exhibiting some deterioration in off-state leakage current, subthreshold swing, and drain-induced-barrier-lowering. Using Germanium leads to relative performance degradation in input capacitance, gate-drain capacitance, and output conductance than silicon. However, Ge shows higher transconductance reduces intrinsic delay and improves intrinsic gain, unit-gain cut-off frequency, and gain-bandwidth product.

articleTitle: ASIC Design of an Interval Type-2 Fuzzy Logic Engine for Control Application
abstract: Despite the existence of VLSI engines for inference generation using type-1 fuzzy sets, little is known about (interval) type-2 fuzzy VLSI engines. An ASIC-based type-2 fuzzy inference engine that was created in two stages is presented in this work. A traditional state-machine method is used in the first stage to construct the control logic and dataflow pathways. In order to verify time restrictions and enhance circuit performance, the inference engine is synthesized on an FPGA in the second stage. Synopsys Design Compiler is used to realize the final hardware implementation. When compared to current implementations, the suggested design performs better in terms of processing speed, resource usage, and inference accuracy. Our method overcomes the drawbacks of current type-1 fuzzy hardware and provides a scalable and effective solution for real-time fuzzy inference applications.

Author Keywords: Interval type-2 fuzzy sets and inference generation

articleTitle: Use of ANNs for Optimizing the Design Parameters of GaN IMPATT Sources
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach for optimizing the design of GaN-based Terahertz (THz) IMPATT sources using Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs). Traditional optimization methods relying on the self-consistent quantum drift-diffusion (SCQDD) model are computationally intensive and time-consuming. By training ANN models on SCQDD-based simulation data, we predict key performance metrics, including RF power output and DC-to-RF conversion efficiency, for GaN IMPATT diodes with different doping profiles. The ANN models demonstrated high accuracy in comparison to experimental data. Additionally, inverse ANN models were developed to optimize diode design based on desired performance targets, significantly reducing computational cost and time. This ANN-based approach enables efficient optimization of GaN IMPATT diodes across a wide frequency range, including THz, offering a scalable solution for the rapid development of high-performance THz radiation sources.

articleTitle: A Low-profile Dual Circularly Polarized Strip Line Feed Antenna with wide Axial Ratio Bandwidth
abstract: This paper proposes a simple low-profile dual circularly polarized (CP) strip line-based feed monopole antenna with wide axial ratio (AR) bandwidth. A microstrip line is printed on the top side of an FR-4 substrate, and a wide-slotted ground with a metallic strip is printed on the other side of that substrate. The orthogonal placement of microstrip feed line and the metallic strip of the ground plane helps to generate dual CP radiation. This simple structure of the proposed CP antenna offers an impedance bandwidth (IBW) of 19.40% (4.84GHz to 5.88 GHz), and ARBW of 39.02% (4.62GHz to 6.86 GHz), covering the wide range of sub-6 GHz band. Furthermore, it exhibits dual CP radiations (both LHCP and RHCP) across the operating band, which is the key feature of the proposed antenna. This simple structure of dual CP antenna can be widely used in navigational applications.

articleTitle: Analytical Modeling of the Ultra Short Channel Negative Capacitance Tunnel FET in Sub-Threshold Regime
abstract: This study explores the feasibility of utilizing a Negative Capacitance Double Gate Tunnel FET (NC-TFET) for energy-efficient digital logic implementations in the sub-threshold regime. A detailed analytical model for the drain current, incorporating the effects of band-to-band tunnelling (BTBT), has been developed and analyzed along with the subthreshold slope (SS). The optimized device demonstrates a notable ON current (~0.024 µA/µm at 250mV) and a Sub-threshold slope (SS) ranging between 12mV/dec and 22mV/dec while maintaining an extremely low OFF current (~fA/µm). The proposed model has been validated using SILVACO ATLAS and MATLAB simulations. This comprehensive analytical modelling suggests that NC-DGTFET is a promising candidate for energy-efficient digital logic circuit design in the subthreshold regime

articleTitle: Impact of Sensing Performance on Junction Less Stack Gate All-Around Metal Oxide Semiconductor Field Effect Transistor for Biosensing Application
abstract: High-performance Junctionless Stack Gate All Around Metal Oxide Semiconductor Effect Transistor (JLS-GAA-MOSFET) biosensor is proposed for the detection of neutral and charged biomolecules. An InGaAs/InP hetero channel dual material stack gate is implemented for the identification of different biomolecules using a 2D ATLAS device simulator. The JLS-GAA-MOSFET biosensor is designed to analyze the various sensitivity parameters by taking both neutral biomolecules like (Uricase = 1,54, streptavidin = 2.1, APTES = 3.57, Ferro Chrome C = 4.7 and Keratin = 8) and charge biomolecules. The sensing behavior of the proposed biosensor is measured by parameter matrix like electrostatic potential, drain current, current, and sensitivity. The JLS-GAA-MOSFET biosensor achieves an optimum value of drain current 0.11mA, and current and threshold voltage sensitivity are 1.69 and 0.455 respectively for Keratin.

articleTitle: RF and Circuit Performance Study of InGaAs Core-shell FinFET
abstract: Detailed device simulations reveal compelling performance advantages for core-shell III-V FinFETs over their bulk counterparts. Our analysis, comparing DC, analog, and RF characteristics, demonstrates that incorporating a silicon core into the InGaAs FinFET significantly boosts electrostatic integrity and analog performance. Notably, the core-shell design exhibits a high transconductance frequency product (TFP) and gain frequency product (GFP), making it highly attractive for high-frequency applications. Furthermore, the core-shell FinFET’s enhanced linearity translates to less signal distortion, a critical factor for maintaining signal fidelity. The circuit implementation of core-shell and bulk FinFET in the form of a resistive load inverter is studied.

articleTitle: Hardware-Efficient VLSI Implementation of Self-Attention Transformers for Natural Language Processing
abstract: This paper presents an optimized VLSI architecture for implementing transformer-based neural networks with emphasis on hardware efficiency and reduced computational complexity. The proposed design features a six layered architecture with a novel 512-dimensional processing unit utilizing an innovative matrix computation approach that achieves significant power savings. Our implementation leverages CORDIC (COordinate Rotation DIgital Computer) architecture to efficiently compute the trigonometric functions required for positional encoding in the transformer model. The design incorporates two specialized CORDIC modules: one configured in rotation mode for sine/cosine calculations, and another in vectoring mode for division operations, both crucial for positional encoding and softmax computations respectively. The architecture is implemented on Vitrex Ultrascale+ VU37P FPGA which demonstrates improved resource utilization through specialized matrix multiplication units while maintaining the model’s core functionality for natural language processing tasks. The implementation achieves a 30% reduction in power consumption and LUT utilization compared to conventional implementations reduced over 48%.

articleTitle: Chaotic Artificial Rabbit Optimization to optimize non linear distributed generation penetration considering harmonic distortion
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization problem aimed at determining the optimal number of DGs to maximize the penetration level of distributed generation (DG). The chaotic artificial rabbit optimization (CARO) method, an improved variant of the original ARO algorithm, has been suggested as a solution. The strategy minimizes active power loss by DG units in the best possible locations, with the best power factor and sizes. Several problems, including harmonic distortion from the non-linear currents injected by non-linear DG (NLDG)devices, limit the amount of DG penetration. The IEEE-519 standard specifies these limitations, which include a power balancing equation, bus voltage limits, and individual and total harmonic distortion limits. On the RDN 118 bus, this suggested method has been tested. The results of CARO have been contrasted with those of the regular ARO algorithm and other techniques found in the literature.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of Dual-Source Vertical TFETs: Comparing Overlapped and Non-Overlapped Channel Architectures
abstract: This work presents the device-level design and performance analysis of Vertical Tunnel Field-Effect Transistors with Double Source (DS-VTFETs). Additionally, the study includes a comparison of two configurations: one with a channel overlap and the other without, highlighting their distinct performance characteristics. The introduction of a channel overlap is intended to enhance some specific device characteristics, leading to improved overall performance. The analysis shows that Dual Source Vertical Tunnel Field-Effect Transistors with overlapped structure depicts superior performance, achieving a high drive current (ION = 1.20 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> A/µm) improvement of approximately 21.32%, a reduction in off-state current (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OFF</inf> = 3.95 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-14</sup> A/µm) by 86.65%, a subthreshold slope (SS =11 mV/decade) improvement of 13.87%, and an average subthreshold slope (AVSS = 35.30 mV/decade ) improvement of 10.43% as compared to the non-overlapped structure. The technique used here provides more control over the electrical properties of the device. These findings highlight the potential of the overlapped DS-VTFET for achieving enhanced performance in current and subthreshold characteristics.

articleTitle: Performance comparison of Photovoltaic sources based multilevel inverters in smart grid
abstract: Multilevel inverters (MLIs) and photovoltaic (PV) sources in coordination improves smart grid performance. This paper evaluates the performance of PV-based MLIs in terms of efficiency, reliability, and power quality. Diode-clamped, flying capacitor, and cascaded H-bridge inverters are among the MLI topologies that are examined and contrasted under various operating circumstances. Parameters are compared to select the best suited topology for the work. To ascertain their appropriateness for smart grid applications, crucial performance indicators are evaluated, including complete distortion of harmonics, switching losses, and overall system efficiency. The impact of dynamic PV generation, grid interaction, and load variations on the inverter performance is also explored. The power conversion quality and operational stability of smart grids are greatly impacted by the MLI topology selection. This study provides insights into the optimal selection and design of PV-based MLIs to enhance the sustainability and efficiency of modern smart grid systems.

articleTitle: Design of a 3-bit Full Custom Flash ADC Using Skywater 130nm PDK for Real Time Control Systems
abstract: This paper demonstrates the design and implementation of a 3-bit flash analog-to-digital converter (ADC), which is fabricated using the Skywater 130nm Process Design Kit (PDK) for real-time control applications. This ADC is designed considering the requirements of applications such as motor control, robotics, and industrial control where fast and accurate signal conversion is needed. The ADC operates within a voltage supply of 1.8V and is able to perform a 3-bit resolution over a range of input voltages from 0 to 1.8V; this allows the ADC to be compatible with many modern mixed-signal control systems. The design provides a versatile approach by having a small layout that has a silicon area of 500 uM x 300 uM. The proposed architecture makes use of 1.8V CMOS transistors in their circuits, including high-speed comparators and a resistor ladder network, ensuring low-voltage performance. It has a solid six-pin arrangement that assists in real-time system designs. This design includes two power (VDD) and ground (VSS) pins. Then it goes on to explain the results associated with the six-pin configuration, confirming that ADCs trade off between speed and VAC cool time. Last but not least, this component can be a control sensing unit in fast control systems, minimizing power use while providing vitally enabled signal output regarding time-sensitive elements.

articleTitle: Surface Plasmon Enhanced Light-Emitting Diode with Hybrid Microcavity Spacing
abstract: The light emission of LED structures can be enhanced by coupling to surface plasmons by using a periodic pattern formed on the top semitransparent metal layer resulting in microcavities. The improved light emission results from trapping of pump photons within the microcavity. The spacing between the microcavities has a strong impact on the light emission characteristics. In this paper, the LED structure with hybrid pattern of spacing interval is developed. The spacing between the silver stripes is same on both the ends in the top layer whereas the spacing between the middle two stripes are kept wider. The electromagnetic field distribution for TE and TM modes is investigated for this approach and compared with the structure of uniform spacing interval. Results show that there is an improvement in the field distribution in TE mode in the structure with hybrid spacing interval when compared with the structure with uniform interval.

articleTitle: Reliability Study of Differential Flip-Flops with Static Contention-Free Characteristics and Redundant Transition-Free Change Sensing for Low-Power Applications
abstract: This study explores the performance and reliability of Differential Flip-Flops (FFs) with contention-free static characteristics & redundant transition-free Change sensing for future low-power & low-voltage applications. The circuit is designed with 16 nm CMOS technology with 0.7 V of power supply (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DD</inf>). We also studied the temperature (T) effect on the behavior of this differential FF with redundant transition-free characteristics. On top fit, we analyzed the performance of this FF in terms of power & delay. In addition to it, we examined the V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DD</inf> scaling effects on this flip-flop performance by changing the V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DD</inf> from 0.7 V to 1.2 V. Finally, we also explored the influence of transistor size downscaling on the D flip-flop performance and this work is carried out using SPICE tools. This flip flop is emerged as a key technology for future internet of things (IoT) Applications.

articleTitle: Low-power and High-speed CNTFET based Four-bit Static Approximate Modified Mirror Ripple Carry Adder for Image Processing
abstract: Several high-speed and low-power computing applications benefit from the approximate computing paradigm that promises a reduction in propagation delay and power consumption but at the same time produces a few erroneous outputs. In this work, an approximate full-adder circuit, which has been implemented by means of logic simplification, has been considered. It has been used to design a four-bit static approximate modified mirror ripple carry adder. The proposed circuit is simulated using 32 nm CNTFET devices on the Cadence Virtuoso tool, which delivers power of 22.47 nW, maximum propagation delay of 34.27 ps, PDP of 7.70 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-19</sup> J, and EDP of 26.39 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-30</sup> Js. Furthermore, to evaluate the effectiveness of this circuit for image processing applications, it has been tested for image sharpening. The output image exhibits a peak signal-to-noise ratio and structural similarity index of 29.88 dB and 0.91, respectively, which makes this approximate circuit ideal for image processing applications.

articleTitle: Radar-based Drone detection using ML techniques
abstract: This work proposes a novel way of using Machine Learning (ML) algorithms on publicly available radar dataset* for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV) detection that contains their Radar Cross Section (RCS) measurement and few other features, in detecting the frequency between 26-40GHz, using Decision Tree algorithm. The dataset measurements were conducted for the quasi-monostatic situation, where the transmitter and receiver are situated in the same position, in an anechoic space. The data demonstrates the manner in which radar waves are dispersed by various UAVs within the designated frequency range. ML algorithms have been used to predict the frequency (GHz) using phi (deg) for x-axis rotation, theta (deg) for y-axis rotation, RCS (dB) as the input parameters. All the results have been implemented in MATLAB.

articleTitle: A Raised Source Drain DG JLFET for Electric Vehicles: Enhancing Performance and Efficiency
abstract: As the transportation sector moves towards electrification, the development of power electronic components becomes increasingly important, with MOSFETs playing a crucial role in electric and hybrid vehicles (EHVs). Raised Source Drain Double Gate Junctionless Field Effect Transistor (RSD-DG JLFET) simulation study is presented here. The study compares the electrical properties of an RSD-DG JLFET with PMOSFET and JLFET. A 2D device simulation platform is used to compare the subthreshold swing, threshold voltage, and Ion/Ioff ratio of the proposed structure, PMOSFET, and JLFET. The simulation results indicate that the RSD-DG JLFET offers significant improvements in efficiency and reliability for EV applications.

articleTitle: Breast Cancer Detection using T-gated Reconfigurable Field Effect Transistor-based Biosensor
abstract: This work introduces a T-gate cavity with drain electrode beneath program gate reconfigurable FET (TCDP-RFET) biosensor for breast cancer cell detection. The T-gate near the source improves biomolecule accessibility, enhancing gate-to-channel coupling, whereas reconfigurability allows it to operate in both p-mode and n-mode. The drain electrode beneath program gate effectively surpasses ambipolarity, improving detection reliability. The dual-cavity structure ensures precise biomolecule immobilization, enabling detection of MCF-10A and T47D cancer cells based on distinct dielectric properties. Simulation demomstrates I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf> sensitivities of 12,256 in p-mode and 6,920 in n-mode, outperforming GaAs-GAAE-FET and DM-DPDG-TFET biosensors by 1471% and 2351% enhancement, respectively. These advancements establish TCDP-RFET biosensor as a superior, highly -sensitive biosensor, paving the way for real-time, label-free cancer diagnostics.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Compact Circularly Polarized Broadband mm-Wave Antenna for Indoor IoT Applications
abstract: The demand for low-profile broadband antennas that generate CP is increasing, especially for portable and handheld devices, as CP antennas help reduce issues like multipath interference and misalignment. To meet this demand, this article introduces a miniaturized mm-Wave antenna. The design features a novel circular labyrinth maze structure, which consists of a central circular ring and two semi-circular patches. The circular ring is etched with eight T-shaped slots at a 45° angle. The current fed to the circular patch splits into right and left directions, and the T-shaped slots offer a return path for the current with a ±90°differential phase, thus producing circular polarization. The design and analysis of the structure are performed using HFSS v.2024.R1 software. The proposed antenna offers an impedance bandwidth of 13.5 GHz (27.1 to 40.6 GHz), a 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth of 8.08 GHz (30.1 to 38.18 GHz), a maximum gain of 7.47 dBi and radiation efficiency of 97%.

articleTitle: Optimized PI/PD/PID Controller Design for DC Motor Speed Control: A Comparative Study of Random Forest-Based Tuning & Classical Methods
abstract: This Study explores ways to improve the speed of DC motors through comparison of traditional tuning methods, viz. Ziegler-Nichols and Cohen-Coon with a machine learning approach using Random Forest. The paper focuses on tuning three types of controllers, PI, PD, and PID to achieve better system performance by reducing errors and achieving stability within the system. The DC motor behavior can be represented mathematically, and the performance of the controllers is evaluated using key parameters such as rise time, settling time, steady-state error, and other error measures. The results show that while Random Forest can predict system behavior fairly well, the traditional methods are more effective in minimizing errors and optimizing the performance of the system. The overall best performance was given by the PID controller. This research gives the value of classical tuning methods, meanwhile bringing evidence of the potential from machine learning to further improve DC motor control.

articleTitle: Comparison and Analysis of Dynamic Comparator Using LECTOR and GALEOR Techniques with 180nm and 45nm Technologies
abstract: This paper introduces a low-power dynamic CMOS comparator designed using 45nm and 180nm technology, which operates at different voltages. To achieve optimal performance, we employ novel circuit design techniques such as the LECTOR (Leakage Control Transistor) and GALEOR(Gate Leakage Transistor). By incorporating leakage-control transistors within the active-high (PUP) and active-low (PDN) networks, we eliminate critical paths and significantly reduce leakage current compared to traditional designs. Our approach leverages the principle of multiple transistors off-states to minimize power consumption. The proposed comparator is evaluated in terms of power dissipation and delay, demonstrating substantial improvements over existing solutions. This paper analyzes the designs of LECTOR and GALEOR comparators, both of which provide significant advantages in power and delay optimization. LECTOR achieves a balanced improvement by reducing power consumption by 13-23% while maintaining efficient delay performance, particularly at higher voltage levels. On the other hand, GALEOR excels in power efficiency, offering remarkable savings of over 96%, making it highly suitable for ultra-low-power applications. Together, these designs present versatile solutions that enhance efficiency in modern electronic systems, catering to various needs in power-sensitive and performance-driven applications.

articleTitle: Design of Dual Gate Mixer with Ambipolar Virtual Source Graphene Field Effect Transistor
abstract: A single-ended resistive mixer based on the ambipolar virtual source Graphene Field Effect Transistor (GFET) with 650 nm technology is designed and analyzed in this article. The dual gate GFET mixer is biased at the gate terminal with different gate voltages so that the intermodulation distortion (IMD) generated by the GFET devices is combined. Due to the different biased conditions of the GFET devices, the linearity of the mixer is improved. The mixer is designed for the 2.4 GHz ISM band, which is unlicensed to 11 MHz of intermediate frequency with a local oscillator frequency of 3.89 GHz for down conversion. The proposed GFET mixer shows a conversion loss of 24.77dB at the 1 dB compression point, and the third order intermodulation is calculated as 28.52 dBc.

articleTitle: Optimizing Power Consumption: CSD-Based 16-Bit Multiplier for Low-Power Systems
abstract: This work introduces a new design of a 16-bit multiplier based on a Canonical Signed Digit (CSD) representation, optimized for low-power implementations. The design reduces switching activity by a great extent, which leads to a significant 99.4% power saving when compared to traditional Vedic multipliers. Reducing the number of non-zero bits in the CSD representation minimizes the number of partial products, which leads to reduced dynamic power consumption. Experimental results prove that the design reduces delay by 82%, with a competitive slice utilization. This work sets a new standard for energy-efficient multipliers, and it is suitable for resource-limited systems like IoT devices and real-time DSP applications.

articleTitle: Decoding Emotions: Facial Expression Recognition and Semantic Rating Prediction with Deep Learning
abstract: This work comprises of three studies. We use the Japanese Female Facial Expression (JAFFE) dataset, comprising of 213 images of 10 Japanese female subjects, depicting six primary emotions: Happy, Sad, Surprised, Angry, Disgust, and Fear, to conduct three different studies. In the first study, we developed a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model to classify major human facial expressions using only the image data. To facilitate this, we constructed a dataset in CSV format containing two columns: the image file names and t heir corresponding expressions, which were encoded based on the naming convention of the dataset. Our model achieved a testing accuracy of 97.08%, demonstrating its effectiveness in recognizing facial expressions. In our second and third studies, we focused on predicting individual ratings for the expressions using the semantic ratings provided in the accompanying text file. These ratings were derived from psychological evaluations on a 5-point scale for the six emotions. We developed a multi-class regression CNN model to quantify these ratings. The second study included all six expressions and yielded a testing accuracy of 75.82%, while the third study, which excluded the expression of Fear, achieved a higher testing accuracy of 86.06%. These findings suggest that Fear may be processed differently from the other basic facial expressions, consistent with observations in psychological studies. This work highlights the potential of using deep learning techniques to quantify and understand the subtle distinctions of human facial expressions.

articleTitle: Optimized Decoupling Capacitor Estimation and Allocation for Supply Noise Reduction in SoC using Soft Computing and Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: In today’s VLSI design, the number of transistors has increased significantly. Implementing an efficient PDN is becoming a difficult issue with very high packing density designs. With ultra-high switching frequencies also contributes to variation of voltages in the electrical nodes, which contributes to supply noise. This noise voltage may result in malfunctioning of the integrated circuit. Therefore, reduction of supply noise is a major concern in system-on-chip. In this work PSN has been optimized using decoupling capacitors. The decap has been optimized using SOS and KNN algorithms. Finally, the integrated circuit has been portioned using pruning technique, floor planning using PSO algorithm and routing has been done using TSP algorithm. Simulation results show there has been overall improvement in the performance of the test circuits.

articleTitle: An Efficient Object Tracking on Edge Devices with Quantized Siamese Networks
abstract: Object tracking on embedded systems requires efficient models that operate within limited computational resources. Edge deployment reduces latency and power consumption, ensuring optimal performance for real-time applications in constrained environments. In this work, we propose a lightweight custom object tracker based on Siamese architecture, optimized for faster response and lower computation. We explore quantization-aware training (QAT) to reduce parameters in the backbone classifier. The tracker, validated on the VOT 2015 benchmark, shows minimal deviation compared to the baseline SiamFC. The tracker was implemented and tested across various platforms, including CPU, NVIDIA Jetson GPU, and PYNQ-Z2 FPGA, demonstrating efficient performance on resource-limited devices while maintaining real-time capabilities. Our compressed model is 2.1× smaller, with minimal accuracy loss, making it suitable for applications such as UAVs, traffic monitoring, real-time surveillance systems.

articleTitle: FPGA Implementation of Transposed FIR Filter for De-Noising ECG Signals
abstract: An Electrocardiogram (ECG) is a bioelectrical signal that represents the heart's condition by capturing its potential changes. It is a commonly used technique for the early detection and assessment of cardiovascular disease (CVD). However, various types of noise can interfere with the ECG signal during recording, potentially leading to an inaccurate diagnosis. This paper describes the design of an effective ECG denoising method implemented in an FPGA. The design is realized with a transposed FIR filter based on a Vedic multiplier and a Carry Select Adder (CSA) and implemented on an FPGA. FPGAs are reconfigurable and reprogrammable in nature and hence are the best choice for such applications. The transposed FIR filter is chosen for its linear phase response and design flexibility, making it highly suitable for high-performance applications with minimal resource utilization. The proposed design incorporates a high-speed multiplier-accumulator unit and utilizes on-chip memory for rapid access to filter coefficients, significantly enhancing computational efficiency. Simulations and synthesis were performed using MATLAB and Vivado 2022.2. The results demonstrate a substantial improvement in the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and a significant reduction in artifacts, leading to clearer and more accurate ECG signal interpretation. The proposed filter achieves lower power consumption, reduced latency, and improved operational efficiency, making it ideal for real-time ECG monitoring.

articleTitle: A Statistical Approach to Analyze the Impact of Random Discrete Dopant (RDD) and Oxide Thickness Variation (OTV) on the Performance of a Low Power Folded Cascode OTA
abstract: The proposed work endeavours to present a statistical study to determine the nature of variation of the major performance parameter i.e. voltage gain of a low power Folded Cascode Operational Transconductance Amplifier (OTA) subject to variations of the two major process parameters—threshold voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</inf>) and gate oxide thickness (t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ox</inf>). The process parameter variations are considered to follow a normal distribution about a mean value with a 3% standard deviation. The OTA circuit is simulated in Spice environment using Python script to generate the entire data set for V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</inf> and t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ox</inf> variations. The OTA gain from the generated data set is analyzed statistically using R programming to determine its nature of variation and is compared with three standard distributions: normal, lognormal and Weibull. The study reveals that the nature of variation of OTA gain due to V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</inf> variation follows a normal distribution where OTA gain due to t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ox</inf> variation follows a Weibull distribution.

articleTitle: Parity based Error Correction Code for Embedded Memories

authors.preferredName: Surya. V. N. S. V. Chakka

abstract: Modern technology is rapidly evolving; modern circuits are becoming more optimized and complex, enabling higher processing speeds and increased storage capacities. However, as electronic devices shrink in size, they become more susceptible to faults, particularly in radiation-intensive environments and extreme temperatures. One major concern in memory systems in modern technology is the data corruption caused by charged particles, which are leading to transient faults that affect system reliability. In this work, a novel Error Correction Code (ECC) method has been introduced, specifically the parity-based ECC, which has a high rate of detecting and correcting the burst errors. This design was implemented using Verilog and synthesized using the Cadence tool on a 45-nm technology node. The proposed ECC can correct up to 4-bit adjacent and non-adjacent errors for 16-bit data and 8-bit adjacent and non-adjacent errors for 32-bit data. The experimental results showed that the error correction code corrects 100% of quadruple adjacent error and 8-bit adjacent error bits. In addition, the area and power consumption as shown considerable reduction when compared to two other existing works.

articleTitle: Simulation Insights of AlGaN/GaN HEMT Structure Optimization for Biosensor Applications
abstract: This article examines the effects of gate-to-drain length (L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GD</inf>), source-to-gate length (L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SG</inf>), gate length (L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</inf>), and environmental conditions like temperature on transfer, transconductance, and output characteristics of HEMT. The Silvaco Atlas device simulation tool was used to retrieve the results. As temperature, source-to-gate length, and gate length grow, peak transconductance, drain saturation current and device ON current decrease. As gate-to-drain length increases, so do peak transconductance, drain saturation current, and device ON current. Variations in the device's L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</inf>, L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SG</inf>, L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GD</inf>, and environmental conditions like temperature alter the device's current characteristics, which can be utilized as a biosensor sensing metric. HEMT-based biosensors, like AlGaN/GaN MOSHEMTs, are highly sensitive to device geometry (L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</inf>, L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SG</inf>, and L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GD</inf>). All these factors contribute to the overall detection accuracy, sensitivity, response time, and power consumption.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Electrical Parameters in GaN-based GAAFETs
abstract: Gallium Nitride (GaN)-based Gate Stack (GS) Gate-All-Around Field Effect Transistors (GAAFETs) are emerging as highly promising solutions for future energy-efficient electronic devices due to their remarkable material characteristics, including high electron mobility, a wide bandgap, and excellent thermal stability. This research emphasizes the evaluation of DC performance metrics for GaN-based GAAFETs, incorporating high-k dielectric spacers and gate underlap techniques. The DC study analyses key parameters such as On-Current, leakage current, switching speed, and subthreshold swing (SS). The results highlight the advantages of employing high-k spacers and underlap designs in GaN-based GAAFETs for low-power, high-performance applications in sustainable and energy-efficient electronics, especially for IoT and 5G systems. The integration of gate underlap with high-k dielectric materials in the spacer region effectively mitigates short-channel effects (SCEs). These findings demonstrate that the proposed design offers notable enhancements in device performance, making it an excellent candidate for next-generation digital and RF applications.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of XOR Implementation using CMOS Logic, Domino Logic - Keeper Technique
abstract: As technology continues to scale and advance, achieving the primary goals of design i.e., low power consumption and faster circuitry have become more feasible. The continuous advancement of technology scaling enables significant reductions in power consumption, a critical objective in digital logic design. Power consumption in digital circuits primarily depends on factors such as supply voltage, the number of transistors used, and transistor scaling. While CMOS technology predominantly relies on inversion logic using NAND and NOR structures, alternative logic design methodologies can optimize transistor usage. Traditional XOR gate designs require multiple transistors; however, this paper presents methodologies for 2-input XOR and 4-input XOR gate implementations using CMOS logic, Domino logic (Keeper Technique) in 90nm technology. The proposed Domino Logic design achieves reduced power consumption compared to conventional CMOS XOR implementations.

articleTitle: Low-PDP 7:3-Counter with Novel Multi-threshold 2:1-Multiplexer
abstract: Current endeavour unfolds a clever design strategy to achieve low-PDP 7:3-counter using novel multi-threshold 2:1-Multiplexer for efficient multiplication. The idea is verified by constructing gate-level circuit with DSCH3.1 first and corresponding transistor-level circuit is designed next on 45nm PDK with BSIM4 technology parameters using Tanner EDA S-Edit. The 1100m-V is the main supply for the design and is excited with every possible custom bit-pattern using v-bit input source of Tanner-EDA to validate. The layout of proposed counter is constructed with 45-nm SPDM CMOS process technology and is evaluated through post-layout transient simulation in all three design corner (i.e. TT, SS and FF) applying 10k random test-patterns at room temperature. The PDP (Power-Delay-Product) is the crucial FOM for digital circuit and that has been measured and benchmarked with some recent competitive designs under same sets of test-pattern@125MHz data rate and in identical operating environment.

articleTitle: Design of High Performance Scan D-Flipflop Using TIGFET
abstract: A new power-efficient Scan D flip-flop is proposed using a novel transistor architecture, the Three-Independent- Gate Field Effect Transistor (TIGFET), leveraging TIGFET-10nm technology, that offers its advantage of improved controllability through multiple independent gates. Conventionally the Scan DFF is implemented using FIN- FET technology. But as the size is reduced the leakage current increases, increasing the power consumption. A delay of 100ns is seen in the DFF implemented by FINFET technology. The increased controllability and higher switching rate of TIGFET helps in reducing the leakage current and delay. Thus the TIGFET-based Scan D flip-flop is expected to have power consumption reduced by 77% and transistor count as well as area reduced without compromising on the performance, which makes it an ideal fit for any advanced high-speed low-power digital system. Thus, the benefit of multi-gate control in TIGFETs is taken in this current design to reduce dynamic power consumption yet allow flexible scan enablement needed for DFT applications. The power-delay-area improvements are confirmed through SPICE simulation using Synopsys HSPICE Tool, which establishes TIGFET as a promising candidate for future VLSI technology.

articleTitle: Compact and Scalable Voltage-Controlled Resistors: Programmable Optically Variable Resistors for Enhanced Circuit Precision
abstract: This paper presents a novel Programmable Optically Variable Resistor (POVR) that provides a wide, continuously adjustable resistance range using an LED-LDR (Light Emitting Diode-Light Dependent Resistor) pair, controlled by varying the LED’s forward bias voltage. The POVR addresses limitations of fixed-value resistors, offering greater precision, compactness, and cost-effectiveness over digital potentiometers and motorized rheostats. Experimental results confirm its wide resistance range, low parasitic capacitance, and scalability. Thermal stability and temperature dependence were also investigated, highlighting the need for heat-sinking. The POVR is ideal for applications like transistor biasing and RC circuits, with future improvements aimed at enhancing stability and integrating predictive models.

articleTitle: Harmonic Suppression in a Meander-Loop Dual-Mode Bandpass Filter by using Spurline
abstract: The present article proposes a compact microstrip dual-mode meander-loop resonator bandpass filter for the wireless communication system. The proposed filter has a bandwidth of 0.1 GHz (fractional bandwidth of 4%) and operates at a center frequency of 2.5 GHz. A size reduction of 30% has been achieved for the meander-loop bandpass filter over the conventional square-loop dual-mode bandpass filter. Despite having improved skirt properties in the passband, the meander-loop dual-mode filter suffers from the presence of spurious harmonics. Subsequently, symmetrically folded spurlines have been incorporated into the feed ports of the meander-loop filter to generate multiple transmission zeros in the stopband by utilizing the bandstop nature of the spurline. As a result, an extended stopband up to 3.08f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> (where f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is the center frequency) with a rejection level greater than 30 dB has been obtained in the simulation. Furthermore, the skirt properties of the filter have been enhanced by the creation of two sharp transmission zeros at the passband edges with attenuation levels greater than 42 dB.

articleTitle: Semi-SJ high-k IGBT: An Effective Approach to Increase Breakdown Voltage
abstract: In this paper, we introduce an innovative semi-superjunction (semi-SJ) high-k IGBT that showcases remarkable advancements in Forward breakdown voltage (BVF) compared to traditional semi-SJ IGBTs. Our comprehensive research reveals a substantial enhancement of 23.07% in breakdown voltage, a significant leap that underscores the efficacy of our design. This improvement stems from the meticulous optimization of redistributed electric field lines, which plays a critical role in achieving superior electrical performance. The implications of this work open new avenues for the development of high-efficiency power electronics, paving the way for more robust and reliable devices in various applications.

articleTitle: Fracttional Order Single Balanced Mixer
abstract: This work presents a single balanced mixer topology in 32nm MOS node. The designing has been carried out using conventional and fractional capacitors of a certain fractional order, α. The Theory of fractional calculus has been used in this work to allow higher degree of freedom in circuit design. By analyzing the results, it has been seen that with increase in fractional order, α from 0.52 to 0.67 the peak voltage and current values in the waveforms increase by 25%, keeping all the other circuit parameters the same. Designing of fractional order capacitors (FOC’s) has been done using passive RC ladder structures. The coefficient values of the ladder for different fractional order, α have been determined using MATLAB programing. The novelty of this circuit is variation of mixing obtained by change in fractional orders and pseudo-capacitances employed. Higher fractional order and lower pseudo-capacitance results in greater mixing as has been observed in results of the paper. In comparison to integer topology the fractional version consumes greater power. An increase in power by 37.5% is attributed to the usage of successive parallel combinations of RC ladder circuits that have been used in circuit designing for fractional capacitors. An optimized circuit in terms of power can be obtained by utilizing CNTFET transistors in place of conventional MOS technology nodes.

articleTitle: Effect of Interface Trap Charges on Improved Junctionless Nanowire Field Effect Transistor
abstract: This paper investigates the reliability issues caused by Interface Trap Charges (ITCs) in the Improved Junctionless Nanowire Field Effect Transistor (Improved-JL-NWFET). These fixed localized charges formed at the channel-oxide interface during fabrication due to radiation, stress, process variations, and hot carrier damage, significantly impacting device characteristics. This paper analyzes their effects on key performance parameters and compares results with a conventional JL-NWFET. Both donor (+ve) and acceptor (−ve) ITCs in the channel/gate oxide interface region are examined for their influence on electrical and analog parameters. The results indicate that Improved-JL-NWFET exhibits more immunity against degradation in electrical and analog parameters compared to its conventional counterpart devices in the presence of positive and negative ITCs.

articleTitle: Reliability Study of Nano Scale Baugh Wooley Multiplier for Future Digital Signal Processing Applications
abstract: The multiplier is critical in various domains, including digital-signal-processing (DSP), graphics processing, processors, and VLSI design. Among the multipliers designed for signed arithmetic, the Baugh-Wooley multiplier (BWM) stands out due to its robustness, integration, and efficiency, rendering it particularly suitable for VLSI applications. This research investigates the performance of the BWM within the context of dynamic CMOS technology, which is characterized by high speed, low power consumption, and area efficiency. We conducted simulations of the multiplier across a range of supply voltages from 0.7 V to 1.2 V and temperatures from 27°C to 107°C. The results indicate that at 27°C, the delay falls by 52.6% with an increment in voltage, whereas at 107°C, the decline in delay is 25%. Furthermore, as the voltage increases, power consumption rises between 1% and 7% across the specified voltage range, while performance enhances, achieving a 90% improvement in the power-delay product. Additionally, short-circuit power consumption shows a reduction of up to 97%. In conclusion, the Baugh-Wooley multiplier implemented in dynamic CMOS technology exhibits superior performance and increased operational speed, making it highly promising for applications in digital signal processing, embedded systems, and VLSI implementations.

articleTitle: Design of Low-Latency, Area- and Power-Efficient CORDIC Algorithms for Sine/Cosine Floating-Point Computation
abstract: This article proposed a system that uses the CORDIC algorithm to compute the sine and cosine functions of floating-point parameters in an area and power-efficient manner. In order to maximize hardware area, power consumption, and memory utilization while maintaining high computational accuracy, the proposed method uses approximation adders rather than conventional ripple carry adders. The novelity of this work is the design of a low-latency system and the reduction of area and power consumption. Which is accomplished through architectural optimizations including using DSP blocks in FPGA for improved performance and reducing the amount of memory used for precomputed angles. Compared to the traditional ripple carry adder implementation, which uses 1.78 mW and has a delay of 1.037 ns, the proposed CORDIC design consumes 1.67 mW, has a latency of 0.427 ns, and reduces the cell area by about 8.15%. With an accuracy of 99.967%, this work offers a major breakthrough in CORDIC optimization for embedded systems, especially for applications involving digital signal processing (DSP) and image processing. Performance research indicates that the proposed design offers advantages in hardware area use and power economy while striking a balance between accuracy and performance.

articleTitle: A Study on CNTFET Ternary and Quaternary Logic with Different Supply Voltages
abstract: Arithmetic circuits are essential to many electronic systems, including highly efficient digital signal processors and microprocessors. Many-Valued Logic decreases both the chip surface area and the number of operations needed to construct arithmetic circuits. An effective replacement for MOS transistors (MOSFET) is being investigated: carbon nanotube FETs (CNTFETs). By merging the potentials of Carbon Nanotube FETs next to Many-Valued Logic, a unique design with a high rise in speed and less difficulty may be provided. In this work ternary and quaternary circuits with supply of 0.9, 1.2 and 1.8 average power and delay are calculated using Cadence tool.

articleTitle: Low-Power Multiplier-Less VLSI Design and Implementation of Linear Convolution Using Vedic Mathematics
abstract: We present in this paper on how we can replace the multipliers with basic operations like shifting and addition in the linear convolution method considering ease of implementation, making it ideal for low-power, resource-constrained environments, such as embedded systems and software-based applications. We have implemented the concept of vertical and crosswise multiplication procedure which is an ancient vedic multiplication process by replacing the multiplication property with shift and add operations. The proposed approach in this paper outperforms similar state-of-the-art research work in terms of power consumption as shown in comparative results.

articleTitle: Low-Power CMOS Operational Amplifier Design in 45nm Technology
abstract: Energy-efficient design is the backbone of modern electronics, crucial for portable devices and medical systems where every milliwatt counts. This paper presents the design and simulation of a low-power CMOS operational amplifier (OpAmp) implemented in a CMOS technology node, optimized for applications requiring ultra-low power consumption. Unlike conventional OpAmp designs that operate in strong inversion, this work leverages moderate inversion to achieve a trade-off between power efficiency and gain performance, making it highly suitable for sensor interfaces in wearable health monitoring devices, hearing aids, and telemetry systems. The proposed design features a cascade second stage for boosting the overall gain, a dynamically biased differential input stage for improved efficiency, and current mirrors to optimize tail current, ensuring stable operation at low power budgets. Simulated results in Cadence demonstrate an open-loop gain of 67 dB, a gain-bandwidth product of 2.31 MHz, and a power consumption of only 12.5 µW, showcasing its feasibility for power-sensitive applications. By offering an implementation-based validation of OpAmp performance in the 45 nm node, this work closes the gap between high-tech low-power electronics’ theoretical concepts and real-world applications.

articleTitle: Design of CMOS based Low Power DCO using MT-CMOS technique
abstract: In this paper, analysis of digitally controlled ring oscillators using delay cells is presented with MT-CMOS technique. The logic circuits based on CMOS nanometer technology face challenges like power dissipation and frequency tunning. To address these issues in the design of this DCO circuit, the MT-CMOS technique is used. The proposed 5-bit digitally controlled oscillator (DCO) circuit comprises five delay cells, each constructed using XNOR gates and a PMOS switching network. The work is evaluated in cadence virtuoso using 90nm technology and 1.4V voltage. The new circuit shows better results in power dissipation from (1.119 mW to 1.590 mW) as well as frequency tunning from (19.64 GHz to 64.84 GHz).

articleTitle: Investigation of QCM Sensor coated with Biosynthesized Nanomaterial to detect major volatile in Indian Cumin
abstract: A highly sensitive and selective Quartz Crystal Microbalance (QCM) gas sensor has been developed to detect volatile present in Indian cumin. Fresh rose petals, R. damascena, have been utilized to generate a natural bio-coating material. The pink-colored extract was prepared after cleaning and boiling the petal pieces in Milli-Q water followed by filtration. This extract was used to synthesize gold nanoparticles by mixing it with HAuCl4 solution, resulting in a color change from light yellow to deep pink, indicating nanoparticle formation. The nanoparticles were separated through centrifugation and deposited onto the QCM surface. The sensor fabrication process involved 15 coating cycles, achieving maximum mass deposition, with the initial frequency of 9994862 Hz decreasing by 4352 Hz. Chronogram analysis revealed the mass and frequency variation during the process. The sensors were tested with the volatile compounds in Indian cumin, identified by GC-MS analysis and the sensor is responsive in detecting α-Pinene present in Indian cumin. The biosynthesized sensor had a sensitivity value of 0.1987 Hz/mgL⁻¹ with a high correlation factor (R2 = 0.9917). The results show that the sensor was successfully fabricated by using naturally derived nanomaterials, which presented high sensitivity and reusability. This study therefore points out that biosynthesized nanomaterials can be used as eco-friendly and effective coating materials in sensor development.

articleTitle: Investigation Temperature variation on DC and Analog performance of Gate Stack GNRFET using DFT-based atomic scale Modelling
abstract: This study investigates the impact of temperature on the performance of a Gate-Stacked Graphene Nanoribbon Field-Effect Transistor (GS-GNRFET) using Density Functional Theory (DFT). The Poisson equation is solved using the Semi Empirical (SE) calculator with the Non-Equilibrium Green's Function (NEGF) method. The proposed GS-GNRFET demonstrates a 30% increase in I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf>, 72% reduction in I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">off</inf>, and 12% enhancement in transconductance (g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>), with a higher transmission coefficient than conventional GNRFET. Temperature analysis of the proposed device reveals a 48% decrease in I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf>, 98% reduction in I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf>/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">off</inf>, and 138 times increase in DIBL from 250 K to 350 K, limiting its use in high-temperature environments. However, these findings make the proposed device suitable for low-power computing, cryogenic electronics, and biomedical sensors.

articleTitle: Utilization of Quality of Service in Basic Wireline Telecom Services for enhancing Consumer Satisfaction in Assam region
abstract: This study explores the impact of Quality of Service (QoS) on consumer satisfaction in basic wireline telecom services in Assam, India. The aim of this research is to identify key QoS indicators that influence consumer satisfaction in the region. A qualitative research method is adopted, utilizing secondary data available for public disclosure, including government reports, telecom regulatory authority publications, and consumer feedback from various platforms. The study focuses on understanding how these indicators such as call quality, internet connectivity, customer support response time, and pricing transparency affect the satisfaction levels of consumers in Assam. The findings indicate that call quality and internet reliability are the most critical factors for consumers, followed by effective customer service and pricing fairness. These results highlight the need for telecom providers in Assam to prioritize service improvements in these areas to enhance consumer satisfaction and loyalty. This study offers valuable insights for policy makers and telecom companies to improve service delivery.

articleTitle: Nanomaterial- DNA Base Affinities: Towards Enhanced Biomarker Detection
abstract: Biomarkers are objective indicators of biological processes, playing a pivotal role in early disease detection and diagnosis. The integration of nanotechnology has significantly improved biosensor sensitivity and selectivity by utilizing nanomaterials ranging from 1nm to 100nm. Various nanomaterials, including ceramic, metallic, quantum dots (QDs), carbonaceous, core-shell, semiconductor, polymeric, and magnetic nanoparticles, are widely used in optical biosensors for biomarker detection. Additionally, emerging materials like ruthenium-functionalized cyclodextrin, metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), and graphene offer promising applications. Graphene-based electrochemical biosensors have proven highly effective in cancer detection, particularly in identifying genetic biomarkers linked to DNA mutations. Advanced techniques such as ICE nano-ESI MS facilitate precise lipid biomarker detection. Nanotechnology is transforming biotechnology and materials science by exploring interactions between DNA nucleotide bases and nanomaterials. This study examines the interactions of adenine, thymine, cytosine, and guanine with C20 fullerene and B40 borospherene using the Quantum ATK platform, computing adsorption energies to assess stability. Results indicate that guanine exhibits the highest stability with both nanostructures, followed by adenine, underscoring their potential in biosensing applications. These insights contribute to developing advanced biosensors and drug delivery systems crucial for early disease detection and personalized medicine. Special emphasis is placed on enhancing biomarker detection in resource-limited settings for improved global healthcare accessibility.

articleTitle: Energy and Area-Efficient FIR Filter Architecture for Low-Power EEG Signal Processing
abstract: In order to process any signal efficiently for more realistic brain activity analysis with least power consumption and simplicity of hardware, digital encephalography systems are definitely required. This paper describes an optimized FIR filter architecture designed to improve power efficiency and reduce silicon area, which should make it suitable for real-time electroencephalography applications. It makes use of coefficient optimization, resource-sharing strategies, and lowpower arithmetic units designed to achieve considerable reduction in computational complexity. It uses the architecture to integrate hardware-efficient multipliers, advanced pipelining, and approximate computing techniques, which help to improve the speed and energy efficiency without affecting signal fidelity. Power consumption, area utilization, and processing speed for FPGA and ASIC implementations of the proposed FIR filter were tested and validated. The experimental results have shown that it consumes 40% less power and uses 30% less area compared with conventional FIR filter designs. In addition, the architecture enables adaptive filtering for real-time noise cancellation, thereby enhancing the quality of EEG signal acquisition in biomedical applications. The work contributes to the advancement of digital encephalography systems by offering a scalable and energy-efficient filtering solution suitable for next-generation brain-computer interfaces and portable EEG monitoring devices.

articleTitle: High PSRR CMOS Voltage Reference using DTMOS for IOMT applications
abstract: This paper presents a high PSRR CMOS voltage reference utilizing dynamic threshold MOSFET(DTMOS) technology for Internet of Medical Things applications. The integration of DTMOS technology enhances temperature stability and reduces sensitivity to supply variations, making it highly suitable for low-power medical devices. The circuit employs fewer transistors to effectively reduce power consumption and minimize area, resulting in a more compact and efficient design. The proposed voltage reference is implemented in 180 nm CMOS technology. The proposed circuit attains a temperature coefficient of 43.7 ppm/°C and a PSRR of -85.6 dB at normal human body temperature, ensuring stable operation in biomedical environments. The design operates over a wide temperature range of -55°C to 85°C, making it suitable for diverse medical applications. Additionally, the circuit exhibits a low noise density of 3.9 µV/√Hz at 1 kHz, ensuring minimal interference in precision analog systems.

articleTitle: Gradient Descent-Based Optimization of Hybrid Renewable Energy Systems for Enhanced Stability and Cost Efficiency
abstract: This research optimizes a Hybrid Renewable Energy System (HRES) using Gradient Descent to achieve a stable, cost effective, and efficient energy supply. The proposed methodology integrates solar photovoltaic (PV) systems, wind turbines and battery storage to balance in energy contributions while maintaining voltage and frequency stability. Optimization is shown to significantly improve stability metrics such that voltage stability is 99% and frequency stability is 97%, thus meeting grid standards and maintaining reliable energy delivery under dynamic conditions. This optimized configuration increased solar energy contributions by 33%, reduced battery reliance by 25% and balanced the energy mix. Nevertheless, total energy generation (684 kWh) and efficiency (85.5%) were slightly reduced (639 kWh and 79.88%), respectively, illustrating the tradeoffs of improving system reliability. We conduct comparative analysis and show that Gradient Descent is a computationally efficient and stable optimization technique outperforming traditional heuristic methods such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Genetic Algorithm (GA) in convergence speed and stability. Future research is needed in advanced predictive controls, adaptive learning algorithms, and other renewable sources to fill efficiency gaps and improve system scalability and sustainability.

articleTitle: Fault Simulation Algorithm for Transistor Stuck Fault in VLSI Testing
abstract: In digital integrated circuits, transistor stuck faults are major issues where transistors got either stuck short or stuck open. These faults lead to circuit malfunctions, logic errors, and power inefficiencies particularly in CMOS based digital designs. So detecting these faults is fundamental challenge in VLSI testing and Design for testability (DFT). This paper addresses the detection and simulation of transistor stuck fault. Verilog code of 2x1 multiplexer is written using switch level modelling for faulty as well as fault free design using Xilinx Vivado tool. The minimum test vectors required for stuck short and stuck open has been identified for 100% fault coverage.

articleTitle: CMOS Analog Artificial Neural Network
abstract: This paper focuses on the design and simulation of low power analog artificial neural network (ANN) using 180nm CMOS technology in Cadence Virtuoso. The neurons here are designed in such a manner that they could perform key biological functions, namely multiplication of the signal, summation, and thresholding. The design exploits advantages of analog computation, leading to lower power dissipation and better processing speed in comparison to purely digital implementations. This makes it particularly suitable for real-time applications. Simulations are performed at different process corners for power consumption analysis to ensure the performance of the network, establishing its efficiency for low-power AI solutions. The key design components include Gilbert cell multipliers for weight multiplication and CMOS-based sigmoid activation functions to provide efficient analog alternatives of the traditional digital elements of a neural network.

articleTitle: Design and Characterization of High-Performance Heterojunction Vertical TFET-Based Biosensors With Trench Gate Structure for Higher Sensitivity
abstract: With the ever-growing demand for high-performance biosensors with better sensitivity, TFET-based biosensors are becoming a promising technology in various biomedical and healthcare applications. This study focuses on the design, analysis of characteristics, and performance comparison between a high-performance SiGe/AlGaAs/Si Hetero-junction Dual Source T-shaped Gate Field-plate Vertical TFET (DSTSGFPV-TFET) based structure and a high-performance SiGe/Si Hetero-junction Single-source Trench-gate Vertical TFET (SSTGV-TFET) based structure, tailored for biosensing applications. Compared to some other recently reported TFET-based biosensor designs, the DSTSGFPV structure shows a better On-to-Off device current ratio sensitivity, while the SSTGV structure exhibits a superior threshold voltage sensitivity. All in all, in terms of sensitivity metrics, both the DSTSGFPV and SSTGV TFET structures proposed in this work are highly promising candidates for advanced biosensing applications.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive guide to economic emission dispatch in wind-fossil-fuel power systems using Gold rush optimizer
abstract: For Economic load-dispatch (ELD) in this article, we will introduce a new population-based metaheuristic algorithm approach named Gold rush optimizer (GRO) based on how gold-seekers prospected for gold during the gold rush Era. Nonlinear characteristics of a generator, such as valve point continuity, are considered in the issue. The GRO algorithm is a dependable and effective solution for nonlinear ELD issues. The proposed technique has been built and evaluated in four test systems. The results confirm the suggested algorithm’s potential and effectiveness when compared to other approaches available in the literature. The results are quite encouraging, demonstrating that GRO is an extremely successful optimization strategy for solving a variety of ELD problems.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Approaches for Enhancing Image Classification Accuracy in Medical Imaging
abstract: Medical imaging plays a significant role in diagnosing and treating several disorders, with correct image classification being essential for effective decision-making. Recent advancements in deep learning have substantially boosted the accuracy of photo classification in medical applications. This research investigates state-of-the-art deep learning methodologies such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Transfer learning, and deep neural networks (DNNs) to increase image classification performance. In this, we give a comparative evaluation of different models employing publically available medical imaging datasets, grading them based on accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity. In this paper, the proposed method also highlights the benefits of data upgrading and transfer learning in tackling data scarcity, a key difficulty in medical imaging. Our experimental results indicate that deep learning-based representations may substantially outperform typical techniques, offering exceptional precision in detecting issues. The findings pave the road for future research aiming at further refining deep learning algorithms for beneficial actual medical diagnosis.

articleTitle: CNT-based charge pump with linearly distributed capacitance for rising time improvement
abstract: The demand for energy-efficient, high-speed, and low-power on-chip voltage generation using next-generation devices is crucial in modern integrated systems. In this work, a four-stage cross-coupled CP is designed using Carbon Nanotube Field Effect Transistor (CNTFET) technology. The proposed CP employs a linearly distributed capacitance strategy to enhance rise time and energy efficiency. The slope parameter, a, which ranged from 0 to -0.8, is assessed by simulations utilizing the 32 nm CNTFET model in Cadence Virtuoso. Initially, the results show that CP with a = -0.8 achieves the shortest rise time (2.81μs) and lowest energy consumption (4.90 pJ) at a total capacitance, C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf>, of 10 pF and C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf>/C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf> of 0.01, with C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf> the equivalent load capacitance.
