The proposed CNTFET-based linearly distributed four-stage CP is expected to be employed in non-volatile memory (NVM), and compute-in-memory (CIM) applications.

articleTitle: Optimal PID Control design for FTMS using WOA Optimization technique
abstract: This study investigates the optimal design of a Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller for a Four-Tank Multi-Input Multi-Output (MIMO) system (FTMS) using the Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA). FTMS characterized by its coupling effects and nonlinear dynamics, presents unique control challenges that are addressed through a decoupling strategy. The system’s mathematical model is analyzed and PID parameters are attained using WOA to achieve optimal time-domain performance. Simulation findings show how reliable and efficient the suggested control strategy with improved response time and stability under varying disturbances. The findings underscore the potential of WOA-based PID design for enhancing control performance in complex MIMO systems.

articleTitle: Novel Design Techniques for Energy-Efficient Double-Tail Dynamic Comparators
abstract: This study explores various dynamic comparator and Double-Tail comparator by examining their delay and power characteristics to enhance operational speed. A lot of high-speed ADCs, such flash ADCs, need comparators with tiny chip areas, low power consumption, and high speed. Both the proposed dynamic comparator and the double-tail comparator utilize positive feedback mechanisms to convert analog inputs into fully digital outputs. In order to achieve power efficiency and great speed, designed comparators are proposed by altering low voltage low power comparators circuits action. Within the suggested comparators, system's power consumption and delay period would both be considerably decreased. The simulations are executed in proprietary Custom compiler, H-Spice 14nm FinFET and 32nm CMOS technologies with 1.2V supply voltage. Power consumption of double-tail dynamic comparator (DTDC) is 1.828µW for 32nm and 9.131µW for 14nm. Power and delay has been reduced by using same area as the existing literature. In contrast utilising the comparator with two tails for the suggested comparator for both power usage and wait times have been substantially decreased.

articleTitle: Automatic Filter Health Monitoring in an HVAC System using FPGA based Hardware Accelerator
abstract: Occupants of enclosed residential, commercial, and industrial zones face significant health risks due to factors like temperature, humidity, and dust. In order to provide comfortable living and working environments, humidity ventilation air conditioning (HVAC) systems keep these indoor space elements stable. The air filter reduces the particulate, which improves breathability. Additionally, the filter's condition affects the HVAC system's ability to maintain humidity and temperature. In this paper, we present a novel feature-based machine learning (ML)-based hardware Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) implementation of an air filter health detection system. This implementation examines the sensor's real-time data to determine the state of the air filter. The detection system achieved an impressive accuracy of 96.7% while consuming only 161 mW of dynamic power.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Energy Efficient OLEDs for Flexible Electronics Applications
abstract: Organic Light Emitting Diodes (OLEDs) are a promising technology known for their thin, energy-efficient, and high-quality light emission, making them ideal for displays and lighting applications. Flexible OLEDs, an emerging development from conventional rigid OLEDs, can be integrated into curved or bendable surfaces, enabling new design possibilities in wearable electronics, foldable screens, and innovative lighting solutions. In this work, we designed and simulated a multilayer OLED structure using TCAD (Technology Computer-Aided Design) software, focusing on material selection for the emission layer to optimize energy efficiency and performance. Three candidate materials—Alq<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, PPV, and PFO—were evaluated, with PFO demonstrating superior luminescent power and energy efficiency. Through geometry optimization of the PFO layer, we achieved an energy efficiency of 14.08%, highlighting its potential as a suitable alternative to Alq<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> for flexible OLED applications.

articleTitle: Reduced Hardware Utilization with Enhanced Error Reduction for Arcsine/Arccosine Computation using CORDIC Algorithm through the Utilization of a Look-Up Table
abstract: CORDIC algorithm is an iterative method to achieve vector rotation without using multiplication. The CORDIC uses computationally intensive square root operation to compute the gain compensation that gets included at each iteration later modified as included at the final stage directly or initiated with the coordinate axis leading to hardware inefficiency and introduces error. By contrast the proposed technique introduces a look-up table method that stores precomputed gain compensation values up to certain iterations which address both concerns simultaneously. When compared to the current approximation technique, the proposed approaches minimize error encountered by 50%, area reduction of 75%, and power reduction of 6%, resulting in significant breakthroughs in CORDIC implementation.

articleTitle: Development and Testing of a System for Automated Resistance-Voltage Characterization of Programable Optically Variable Resistors
abstract: An automated system for resistance-voltage (R-V) characterization of programmable optically variable resistors (POVRs) has been developed. It integrates an ESP-32 microcontroller to modulate the forward bias voltage across the POVR’s light emitting diode (LED) sources via pulse-width-modulated (PWM) signals and measure the corresponding resistance of the light-dependent resistor (LDR)-detector. The forward bias voltages are incrementally varied from zero to the LEDs’ rated values. To accommodate the LDR’s resistance range (from a few megaohms to hundreds of ohms), a 1×6 multiplexer circuit with six precision resistors (10 MΩ to 100 Ω, ±1% tolerance) and corresponding transistor switches ensures automatic range selection. The R-V characteristics of POVRs with four spacer lengths were measured both manually and with the automated system. The automated system demonstrated high accuracy, with a mean percentage error below 2.5%, showcasing its reliability and efficiency for POVR characterization.

articleTitle: Optical Lithography Proximity Correction using Machine Learning and Richardson-Lucy Deconvolution
abstract: The proximity effect in optical lithography distorts patterns due to diffraction, scattering, and interference, reducing accuracy and increasing defects. This study combines Machine Learning and iterative deconvolution to enhance pattern precision. A dataset of mask patterns distorted by Gaussian, Sinc, and Airy disk Point Spread Functions trains a model to estimate their contributions. For a sixteen-square pattern with fifteen-micron sides and three-micron spacing, Gaussian blurring causes a 10% area spread prompting proportional decrease. The Richardson-Lucy Deconvolution algorithm refines the pattern by deconvolution, yielding squares with twelve-micron sides and six-micron spacing. Evaluations show improvements with a Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio of 24.1940, Structural Similarity Index of 0.98644, Edge Normalized Cross-Correlation of 0.14976, and Deconvolution Quality factor of 0.99619. This method effectively mitigates proximity effects and enhances mask-writing accuracy.

articleTitle: An Optimal PID Controller for Artificial Knee Exoskeleton Devices
abstract: One may experience knee problems due to several issues, such as arthritic conditions being overweight, strokes, post-polio conditions, ligament damage, or mishaps. To assist in mobility, artificial knee devices are frequently used. In this study, an optimal proportional integral derivative (PID) is proposed with the aim of achieving precise control over the angular movements of these devices. Furthermore, the proposed controller for knee exoskeleton systems is effectively tuned using a well-known metaheuristic algorithm named particle swarm optimizer (PSO). The simulation results demonstrate that PSO-PID controller significantly outperformed traditional algorithms in the area of control performance when employed with the knee exoskeleton systems.

articleTitle: IGZO TFT Based Logic Circuits And Ring Oscillator Design in Verilog-A For Flexible Electronics
abstract: The growing demand for Thin-Film Transistors (TFTs), especially driven by the emergence of flexible electronics, emphasizes the critical need to validate the effectiveness of new thin-film materials for TFT-based circuit design. In response, this paper proposes a comprehensive behavioral model employing compact device modeling, specifically utilizing a Verilog-A Lookup Table model to design the logic circuits using IGZO TFTs. The proposed methodology enables an accurate behavioral representation of TFT behavior for IGZO and various other materials. Simulation and verification of the IGZO TFT circuits were carried out in Pathwave ADS, demonstrating the model's potency in evaluating the performance across a spectrum of digital circuits. In this work, a design of experiment (DOE) simulation has been performed to evaluate the optimal size of the inverter to achieve the high load driving capability of a maximum load of 50uF and lower power-delay product (PDP) of 23.326 pJ. In particular, the optimized inverter was used to design a stable 31-stage ring oscillator. The oscillation frequency range lies between 416.667KHz to 28.49KHz from 3 stages to 31 stages respectively. Overall, this research presents a practical and efficient approach to validate new thin film materials-based circuit design within a minimum time frame and design cycle.

articleTitle: Design of Underlap PDSOI FinFET-Based Capacitorless 1T-DRAM with High-K Spacers for Enhanced Performance
abstract: This work presents the design and simulation of an Underlap PDSOI FinFET based Capacitorless 1T-DRAM with spacers using TCAD simulation tools. In the proposed device, the PDSOI and channel regions of the FinFET act as a floating region, which stores holes for use in the Capacitorless 1T-DRAM application. These holes are primarily generated through high-impact ionization occurring at the channel-drain junction. The PDSOI region is surrounded by a low-k isolation dielectric oxide, providing isolation between the active regions and reducing capacitive coupling between the PDSOI region and the gate electrode. This reduction in coupling improves the device sensing margin. High-k spacers are also used adjacent to gate electrode to reduce the leakage and enhance the retention of the device. By utilizing a single transistor for the DRAM, the complexity of the device is reduced, allowing for higher DRAM density in integrated circuits, which boosts productivity. The proposed device also offers several advantages, including low fabrication costs, low power consumption, a high sensing margin (~132 μA), long retention time (> 1 ms), and fast read/write operations (~10 ns).

articleTitle: Performance assessment of Charge Plasma Triple Metal Gate Junctionless Vertical TFET-based Biosensor using Gate Engineering technique
abstract: The detection of biomolecules using nanoscale devices presents significant challenges due to fabrication complexities and sensitivity limitations. This study suggests a unique Charge Plasma with junctionless Triple Metal Gate Vertical Tunnel Field-Effect Transistor (CP-TMG-JLVTFET) biosensor as a solution to these problems, leveraging gate engineering and dielectric modulation techniques. The biosensor is designed for label-free detection of both neutral and charged biomolecules. Comprehensive simulations using the SILVACO Atlas 2D simulator were performed to evaluate device performance, focusing on critical parameters such as drain current, electric field, and subthreshold swing (SS). Key findings indicate that the proposed device achieves a high sensitivity of 7.33×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sup> for a dielectric constant of k=12, with a significant improvement in the Ion/Ioff ratio and a steep subthreshold swing of 14.5 mV/decade. These results demonstrate the superior sensitivity and detection capabilities of the CP-TMG-JLVTFET biosensor, making it a promising platform for advanced biomolecule detection.

articleTitle: Design of Power-Efficient High-Precision Dual-Mode Adder
abstract: This work presents the design and analysis of low-power arithmetic circuits optimized for approximate computing: the Power Efficient Single Exact Single Approximate (PESESA)-1 and PESESA-2 adders. PESESA-1 preserves exact CARRY calculation with approximate SUM with one error, whereas PESESA-2 approximates the CARRY with exact SUM calculation. The two designs operate in approximation mode for hardware and power efficiency and exact mode for highest accuracy with Power Gating (PG) for minimizing static power consumption. PESESA-1 and PESESA-2 are 34.2% and 25.6% more power-efficient than the mirror adder, respectively. Their efficient design makes them suitable for energy-constrained applications such as signal processing, data compression, and error-resilient computing. Their efficient design ensures a balance between computational accuracy, reduced power dissipation, and simplified circuit complexity, making them adaptable to a wide range of low-power applications.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation for Analog Performance Assessment of Vertically Stacked FeFinFET
abstract: This paper explores the impact of localized charges on the analog performance of Vertically Stacked Ferroelectric FinFET (VS-FeFinFET), integrating advanced technologies like SOI, strained tri-layered channel, and ferroelectric material for improved gate control. It examines how interfacial trap charges (ITCs), induced by radiation or stress, affect device performance. VS-FeFinFET shows improvement in leakage current (Ioff) by 53.1%, switching ratio by 105%, and threshold voltage (Vth) by 9.31% along with significant enhancement in other performance parameters for negative ITCs. By varying ITC’s densities (1 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sup> -1 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">–2</sup>), the study reveals that multifold reduction in Ioff leds to boost in switching ratio by 350% and 1.55 times in Vth with increasing density. These insights aid in optimizing VS-FeFinFET for enhanced reliability and efficiency, shaping next-generation electronics.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Assisted Sensitivity of Triple-Material Gate -Stack Gate-All-Around (TM-GS-GAA) MOSFET based Biosensor
abstract: In this paper, the variation in dielectric of TM-GS-GAA MOSFET device has been considered for the detection of biomolecule. The gate stack has high and low– K dielectric constant. The surface potential and drain current are analysed for high-k gate dielectric materials like TiO2, ZrO2 and Al2O3. The threshold voltage variation and the Ion/Ioff ratio serve as the primary measures for determining sensitivity. Furthermore, the machine learning based decision tree algorithm has been proposed to investigate the sensitivity of biomolecules with variation in nanogap cavity. The mean squared error (mse) and R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-score has been calculated for the proposed algorithm for the explored device. It shows mse as 0.02 and 99 % as R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-score which indicates the proposed algorithm achieved the same accuracy as that of device simulation. The TM-GS-GAA MOSFET based biosensor has been compared with DM-JL MOSFET and shows an excellent enhancement in the sensitivity. The new device is designed for advance biosensing applications, offering innovative solutions for detecting and analysing biological materials.

articleTitle: Assessment of Analog/RF and Linearity Parameters of n-Channel Germanium Nanosheet FETs
abstract: This research examines the analog, RF, and linearity performance of a Germanium nanosheet transistor with a 16nm gate length, comparing it against a similar Silicon nanosheet transistor to assess its viability at these scaled dimensions. While the Germanium device exhibits a higher subthreshold swing due to increased short-channel effects, its higher electron mobility leads to significant improvements in drive current and transconductance. Specifically, the Germanium nanosheet transistor demonstrates 1.7 times greater ON current, 2.75 times higher transconductance, and a 1.71 times improvement in transition frequency compared to the silicon device. These enhancements in current and transconductance also translate to better RF performance, including higher gain-frequency and transconductance-frequency products. However, an analysis of transconductance derivatives reveals that the germanium nanosheet transistor exhibits reduced linearity compared to its silicon counterpart.

articleTitle: Homomorphic Encryption in Quantum Computing
abstract: Homomorphic encryption (HE) is a groundbreaking cryptographic method that allows calculations on encrypted data without the need for decryption, thus safeguarding privacy and security. This article investigates how to implement homomorphic encryption with QISKIT, a free-to-use quantum computing framework. The research investigates the theoretical underpinnings of HE, its use in quantum computing, and its importance for privacy-preserving calculations. Moreover, the study covers adder circuits based on quantum logic gates, their realization with QISKIT, and the prospects for improving computational security in cloud environments. The results stress the practical viability of HE in quantum environments, underscoring its possible uses in secure data processing and privacy-enhancing technologies.

articleTitle: Energy-Efficient 4-Bit Multiplier for High Performance and Low Power Consumption
abstract: Power-efficient multiplier design plays a critical role for enhancing energy efficiency and performance in modern digital systems. This study presents an optimized 4-bit array multiplier using CMOS technology (GPDK 90nm) and a Transmission Gate (TG)-based approach. The design integrates TG-based AND and XOR gates with an enhanced full-adder circuit, ensuring improved signal integrity, reduced power dissipation, and lower propagation delay. Simulations in Cadence Virtuoso show a 61.49% reduction in power dissipation and a 70.97% decrease in delay compared to conventional designs. These results highlight the proposed multiplier's potential as a low-power, high-performance solution for VLSI applications.

articleTitle: Obstacle Avoidance in Routing with GNR Interconnect
abstract: During the routing phase of VLSI physical design, obstacles often arise along the routing paths due to previously established connections or other constraints. These obstacles pose significant challenges for VLSI designers in constructing efficient routing trees that navigate around them. Graphene nanoribbon interconnects, which are limited to bending angles of 0°, 60°, and 120°, further complicate this process. The routing cost for graphene nanoribbon interconnects depends on both the interconnect length and the bending angles involved. In this work, we propose a cost-minimization technique that leverages graphene nanoribbon interconnects to determine optimal routing paths for a given source node, a set of sink terminals, and multiple rectangular obstacles.

articleTitle: Exploration of Interaction Dynamics between Au-doped Graphene and Aliphatic-Aromatic VOCs
abstract: This study aims to examine the electro-chemical properties of toxic VOCs found in industrial effluents viz. ethylene, acetylene, and benzene, and their sensitivity and reactivity towards gold (Au) doped graphene sheet (Au-G). Several electro-chemical properties were evaluated to determine the sensing capabilities, which included the highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO), the lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO), molecular electrostatic potential (MEP), partial density of states (PDOS), band structure, and infrared (IR) spectra for three different cases. Molecular orbital energy gap, MEP, and band structure supported strong reactivity characteristics of benzene and ethylene over Au-G as compared to acetylene. The adsorption characteristics of these gases were analyzed via adsorption energies which was found to be -1.01 eV for ethylene, -0.68 eV for acetylene, and -1.21 eV for benzene, respectively. The findings were further validated by binding distance analysis, electron localization function (ELF) mapping and Mulliken charge analysis. This study also highlights the potential of Au-doped graphene as a gas sensor for detecting these toxic VOCs which have significant environmental and health implications.

articleTitle: GaN Heterostructure-Based MOSHEMT with an Embedded Cavity for Neutral Biomolecule Detection
abstract: This paper presents a GaN-based Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor High-Electron Mobility Transistor (MOSHEMT) integrated with an embedded cavity to detect neutral biomolecules. On the drain side, under the gate, the cavity structure is formed with a length of 500 nm and a depth of 7 nm. The embedded cavity eliminates the need for a reference electrode. The study employs a dielectric modulation approach within the cavity area to replicate the effects of various dielectric biomolecules. The sensitivity of the biosensor to a specific biomolecule is analyzed by examining the changes in the drain current (∆I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DS</inf>) and threshold voltage (∆V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</inf>) with reference to the empty cavity i.e air with a dielectric constant of 1. The MOSHEMT biosensor device structure has been simulated using ATLAS Silvaco simulation tool. The biomolecule kertain has exhibited the highest change of 1.42 V in V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</inf> and 125 mA/mm in I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DS</inf>.

articleTitle: Design of Low Transistor Count Approximate Full Adder with Carry Approximation
abstract: In many digital signal processing (DSP) applications, such as image and speech processing, slight inaccuracies in output data are often tolerable for human interpretation. This may be exploited with approximate computing which allows for reduced computational complexity by using circuits that are intentionally designed to be less precise. By adopting approximate circuits, which require fewer transistors than their exact counterparts, designers can achieve more efficient hardware implementations. In this work, we explore a full adder design that leverages transmission gates to approximate the carry output using the primary inputs A and B. This approach effectively reduces the transistor count and propagation delay from the traditional 28T in accurate full adders to either 16T or 20T, depending on the level of approximation employed.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a High-Stability HS-12T SRAM Cell for Low-Power Applications
abstract: In this paper, the HS-12, a very stable 12T Static Random-Access Memory (SRAM) cell, is designed with better read operation. Traditional 6T SRAM cells suffer from major constraints, especially concerning read stability and power efficiency. To resolve these, the proposed 12T SRAM cell integrates extra transistors that practically separate read and write operations and thereby provide improved read, write, and hold stability. Critical performance indicators like read stability, write stability, power dissipation, and access times are comprehensively examined and contrasted with current SRAM architectures. Simulations with 45nm CMOS technology confirm that the HS-12T SRAM cell displays enhanced resistance to process, voltage, and temperature fluctuations, providing reliable operation under a wide range of conditions. Enhanced reading stability is especially beneficial for those applications with high reliability and low power requirements, like cache memory in handheld and embedded systems. This work offers a promising approach to future SRAM designs, providing an optimal balance between performance, energy efficiency, and robustness, and opens the door to future innovations in memory technology.

articleTitle: Performance Optimized 32-bit Multiplier: Integrating Vedic and Karatsuba Techniques
abstract: Multiplication is a fundamental arithmetic operation widely used in applications like digital signal processing, cryptography, and control systems. This work presents a 32-bit hybrid multiplier that combines Vedic and Karatsuba algorithms to balance speed, area, and power consumption by leveraging the strengths of both methods. The hybrid architecture enhances computational efficiency, making it suitable for real-time applications. By integrating the benefits of Vedic and Karatsuba multipliers, the proposed design achieves optimal metrics in terms of power, speed, and area. Performance analysis shows that the hybrid multiplier reduces delay by 9.76% compared to the standalone Vedic multiplier and 7.94% compared to the Karatsuba multiplier, with minimal variation in power consumption. This makes the hybrid design ideal for high-performance digital systems, demonstrating its superiority over standalone designs in achieving an efficient trade-off across critical performance parameters.

articleTitle: Design of a Flower-Shaped Rectangular Slotted Super Wideband Microstrip Antenna
abstract: This paper presents a compact, flower-shaped antenna design with a rectangular slot, optimized for super wide-band applications. The antenna dimensions are 45 mm×50 mm× 1.6 mm, featuring a microstrip line feed, flower-shaped patches, and a rectangular slot measuring 16 mm × 6 mm. Its design and performance were evaluated using finite element method (FEM) tools, such as HFSS, to ensure excellent performance in terms of bandwidth, impedance matching, radiation pattern, far-field directivity, return loss, and gain.The antenna’s dimensions and materials were optimized through extensive analyses, including variations in layers, materials, and slot sizes. FR4 epoxy was selected as the substrate material for its cost-effectiveness and suitability for high-frequency applications, while copper was used for the patch and ground plane due to its superior conductivity. The antenna achieves minimal return losses across the frequency range of 3.5 GHz to 27 GHz, maintaining a return loss of −10 dB. Additionally, the Bandwidth Dimension Ratio (BDR) is calculated as 10.44 ×1012 Hz/m2, llustrating the efficient utilization of physical dimensions to achieve a wide frequency range, the proposed antenna’s broad operational bandwidth, stable radiation characteristics, and compact size make it a promising candidate for various modern wireless technologies. These include satellite and radar communication, 5G and mmWave systems, ultra-wideband (UWB) communication systems, medical imaging, wireless sensor networks (WSN), cognitive radio-based spectrum sensing, and Internet of Things (IoT) applications.

articleTitle: Image Steganography using LSB technique and VLSI implementation
abstract: Data hiding is an important method for providing secure and undetectable communication in the digital domain, such as images, audio, and video. Least Significant Bit (LSB) data hiding has become one of the widely adopted approaches for embedding information in digital media. In the recent past, many researchers have concentrated on the LSB technique within VLSI design implementation. This paper used LSB-based image hiding method in the HDL coder environment. The system attains superior data accuracy, minimal degradation, and strong resilience, as evidenced by the experimental findings. LSB data hiding built into VLSI technology is the key to solving today's security problems in areas like safe communication, digital watermarking, and copyright protection, offering a solution that can be used by many people and is effective.

articleTitle: A L, S and C-Band Source-Controlled Voltage Variable Attenuator for Beam Control
abstract: This paper demonstrates a source-controlled attenuator, where control voltage is given to the source terminal of the main transistor (MT). The current is being attenuated from reaching the output. Conventional attenuators employ voltage divider principle or phase cancellation technique. In this work, at maximum attenuation, gate-to-source voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">gs</inf>) is less than threshold voltage of the main transistor and hence, no current reaches the output. At minimum attenuation, V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">gs</inf> is greater than threshold voltage and hence, entire current is transferred to the output. The attenuator shows good attenuation flatness, wide bandwidth, good linearity, unconditional stability and low noise figure for control voltages ranging from 0.93 V to 1.23 V with a step of 0.01 V. For fixed load, the attenuator has less than 1 dB amplitude error in the required bands (1.1-1.3 GHz, 2.7-2.9 GHz and 5.4-5.8 GHz). The attenuator can be used in T/R module of phased array radar.

articleTitle: Transmission Gate based Reordered Normal Basis Multiplier
abstract: This paper introduces the Transmission Gate-based Reordered Normal Basis (TGRNB) multiplier, which is a multiplication algorithm used in finite field arithmetic, It is crucial in many cryptographic applications, which aim to improve the performance and efficiency of Reordered Normal Basis (RNB) multiplications. This multiplier is implemented using transmission gates and compared with static CMOS logic. The TGRNB multiplier utilizes transmission gates, which control the flow of signals in the circuit by allowing efficient implementation by reducing power consumption and increasing overall performance. The main advantage of TGRNB multiplier is its ability to perform operations in parallel, leading to significant speed improvements. Hence, this multiplier offers faster operation, higher power efficiency, and better adaptability compared to the static CMOS implementation.

articleTitle: Study of Temperature Dependence on DC/RF Parameters of Extended Channel Gate Stacked Heterojunction TFET
abstract: In this manuscript, a novel Hetero-junction TFET design is proposed, which utilizes a SiGe source and incorporates an extended section of the channel into the source region. This structure is further enhanced by the integration of an n+ pocket doping and a dielectric pocket (DP) at the drain-channel interface. The proposed structure is analyzed using the Sentaurus TCAD simulator in this study. The DP placed at the drain-channel junction depletes the drain region near the interface. This effectively increases the tunneling width at the drain-channel interface, resulting in a significant reduction of ambipolar conduction in the TFET. The suggested TFET reflects a better I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf>/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OFF</inf> ratio of 2.79 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup> and steeper SS of 10.52 mV/dec as well as mitigates ambipolar conduction in negative bias region. Furthermore, the impact of varying temperatures within the range of 300 K to 400 K on different parameters is analyzed. The device’s performance is critically dependent on temperature variation. The bandgap of the semiconductor material changes with temperature variation. The results indicates that the current conduction has minimal temperature dependency, while in ON state but shows a significant rise in OFF state current. Moreover, the study examines the consequences of temperature fluctuations on various analog/RF FOM parameters.

articleTitle: Low and High Frequency Noise Analysis of Si-Ge TFET
abstract: This paper is centered on the assessment of the noise properties of Si-Ge TFETs belonging to both the low-frequency noise (LFN) and high-frequency noise (HFN) regimes through MATLAB simulations. The investigation also focuses on practical applications of insulating materials to reduce noise and improve device efficiency. In LFN, flicker noise is studied up to 10 kHz that is across a frequency range of 10 Hz to 10 kHz using high-k dielectrics Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and ZrO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> has the lowest noise levels, which is a result of low trap density, and consequently, low charge trapping. For HFN, thermal noise characterization is done within the range of 10 kHz to 10 MHz and the result demonstrate flat behavior with platform show the suitability of Si-Ge TFETs for high frequency applications.The obtained outcomes confirm the significance of the choice of material for exhibiting low-noise, stable characteristics which in return makes Si-Ge TFETs effective for low-power and high-speed electronic system applications. Other possibilities for further work are the extension of the device architecture, the exploration of further insulating material and experimental studies of the noise behavior of the device under different operating conditions.

articleTitle: A Review of Ambipolarity Suppression in Tunnel FETs Using Significant Engineering Techniques
abstract: The incapability to lower the subthreshold swing (SS) to less than 60 mV/decade is a major obstacle to the scaling down of traditional Metal Oxide Semiconductor Field Effect Transistors (MOSFETs). Because of its low SS (< 60 mV/dec), low OFF-state leakage, and high I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf>/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OFF</inf> switching current ratio, the Tunnel Field Effect Transistor (TFET) is one of the prospective substitutes for the traditional MOSFET to overcome this limitation. Furthermore, TFET functions as an energy-efficient switch because of its low power consumption. However, ambipolarity and low ON current are issues with TFET. The term "ambipolarity" describes the TFET's dual nature. The ambipolar problem prevents the TFET from being fully turned off for zero gate bias. Thus, its usefulness and viability in complementary digital circuits are limited. There are several engineering techniques to suppress ambipolarity. This work reviews several device approaches to reduce the ambipolarity of TFET.

articleTitle: Simulation of a-IGZO TFT Device Using Finite Element Method
abstract: This work uses the COMSOL Multiphysics simulation tool to analyse the effect on the transfer characteristics of an amorphous indium-gallium-zinc-oxide (a-IGZO) thin film transistor (TFT) due to varying some parameters such as active channel thickness, doping concentration, gate dielectric thickness, and metal electrodes work function (4.2-4.5 eV). We demonstrated that when the thickness of the a-IGZO active layer, gate oxide, and doping concentration increases, the threshold voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</inf>) decreases. The subthreshold swing (SS) and threshold voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</inf>) are the functions of channel layer thickness and gate oxide thickness. Also, we demonstrated the linear shift in threshold voltage due to varying surface charge on the a-IGZO active layer. This ability makes it an ideal choice for sensing applications.

articleTitle: Silicon Carbide based Dielectric Modulated Triple Metal Gate All Around MOSFET (TMGAA) for Enhanced Electrical characteristics and Analog performance
abstract: This manuscript outlines the design and performance analysis of a novel Silicon Carbide (4H-SiC)-based Dielectric-Modulated-Triple-Metal-Gate-All-Around (TMGAA) MOSFET using the ATLAS 3-D structure simulator. A gate-stack incorporating (high-k) dielectric materials, specifically Hafnium Oxide, HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and Aluminum Oxide, Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, has been utilized as the gate dielectric. The proposed TMGAA structure enhances electrostatic control, reduces short-channel effects, and improves charge carrier mobility, leading to superior analog performance. To ensure a fair comparison, the performance characteristics of TMGAA MOSFET have been equated with the structure functionality of the Double-Metal-Gate-All-Around (DMGAA) MOSFET focusing on key analog performance metrics such as drain current, I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ds</inf>, transconductance, g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>, and output conductance, g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf>.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of 180nm Low Noise Amplifier for 2.4GHz Communication Technology
abstract: The LNA is a critical component of the RF front-end circuit, which amplifies weak signals received by the antenna and provides a low-noise signal to the subsequent stages. This paper presents the design and analysis of a low-noise amplifier (LNA) for 2.4 GHz communication systems in TSMC 180nm technology. The common source cascode and common source folded cascode topologies are used to optimize the LNA design for high performance and low power consumption. We discuss the basic design considerations for an LNA, including the noise figure, gain, scattering parameters, and stability, with a systematic optimization. The proposed LNA achieves a gain of 19.83 dB, a noise figure of < 2 dB, and a return loss of -10.192 dB, which meets the requirements for 2.4-GHz communication systems. The designed LNA provides an excellent solution for high-performance, low-noise amplification and can be used in wireless communication systems with stringent requirements for noise, gain, and power consumption.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Stair shaped cavity TFET Based Biosensor
abstract: Tunneling Field Effect Transistor (TFET), due to its lower subthreshold swing, is a promising choice for developing a biosensor with great sensitivity. In this study, we presented a TFET-based biosensor incorporating SiGe material in the source region, a highly doped n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> pocket between the source and the channel, and, for the first time, implemented a stair-shaped cavity design. The proposed configuration enables sensitive detection of both charged and neutral biomolecules. With a novel stair-shaped cavity and a SiGe source with an n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> pocket, our proposed biosensor shows an enhancement in drain current sensitivity. Our simulation results demonstrate an improved sensitivity of 1.4926×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> for neutral biomolecules at K=10 and 1.4043×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> for charged biomolecules at a charge density of ρ=-1×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−11</sup>. In this study, we also conducted a comparative analysis of the performance of the proposed biosensor with the conventional n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>-doped pocket-based TFET biosensor having a uniform cavity. With the first-time non-uniform stair-shaped cavity design in our proposed biosensor, we tried to increase the gate coupling for improved band-to-band tunneling and drain current sensitivity. Therefore, with the enhancement in sensitivity, our research contributes to the ongoing efforts to create highly sensitive, label-free, fast, and accurate biomedical diagnostic tools, paving the way for revolutionary applications in healthcare, biotechnology, and various other industries.

articleTitle: Gallium Nitride Gate-All-Around Macaroni Field Effect Transistor (GaN-GAA-MCFET): Biosensor for DNA detection
abstract: The Gallium Nitride Gate-All-Around Macaroni Field Effect Transistor (GaN-GAA-MCFET), a novel Dielectric Modulated Biosensor specifically engineered for DNA detection, is presented in this paper. The primary objective of gallium nitride semiconductor-based FET biosensor is to improve biosensing performance by combining several device engineering techniques such as channel engineering by using macaroni channel, split gate, and oxide engineering. Three split gates are deployed for gate engineering, and the Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>+HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> stack has been utilized during oxide engineering. The GaN-GAA-MCFET biosensor has two nanocavities which are formed by etching the complete metal and layer of HfO2 in a specific region to make open cavities to boost structural stability and detection sensitivity. For the DNA biomarkers, the proposed design offers an appealing threshold voltage sensitivity in contrast to the several other devices found in the literature.

articleTitle: Solar Energy Focusing Technology Applied in Dual-Function Autoclave for Sterilizing Medical Instruments
abstract: The study presents theoretical and experimental work on a solar system consisting of an autoclave and parabolic dish that produces steam to sterilize medical tools and distilled water. Thermal performance was examined for summer and winter seasons in Hills, Ooty. Different designs of solar autoclaves or distills were compared based on factors such as sun irradiation, ambient temperature, wind speed, and absorption wall temperature. A copper helical conical coil was used for dual performance. The system satisfied sterilization conditions (121C and 2.05 bar) within 10.6 min and 13.4 min in summer and winter, respectively, when the average direct solar irradiance was (1199,700) W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The daily production reached 8.12 L/day and 10.034 L/day on summer and winter seasons, respectively, from 9:00 a.m. to 16:00 p.m. When various solar distills kinds are compared with similar work durations, the results show exceptional performance. Additionally, this system can be deemed acceptable since it satisfies the needs of hospitals and clinics, in rural locations, from steam and freshwater in the event of an electrical blackout and from using inexpensive, readily available materials from local markets.

articleTitle: Resilient Design of a Tilt Integral Derivative Controller with Adaptive Differential Evolution Optimisation and Filter for Frequency Control
abstract: This article focuses on the design of filter-based Tilt Integral Derivative Controller (TIDN) for frequency control of a multi area power system. At first, an identical two area two-unit power system is considered. In which, one unit is thermal and other unit is hydro systems and their first order models are considered. The system is demonstrated by having TIDN as secondary controller for 1.5% of step load variation in area-1. The gains of TIDN controller are evaluated by using Adaptive Differential Evolution (ADE) technique. The supremacy of proposed scheme is also analyzed by comparing with other published results. Additionally, sensitivity analysis of the proposed scheme is also observed for variations of the parameters. From all the dynamic responses it is observed that, the proposed scheme performs better compared to others.

articleTitle: Non-Invasive Glucose Detection via Dual Sensitivity Modified CSRR Sensor Around 2.4 GHz
abstract: This paper introduces a non-invasive dual-sensitivity glucose sensor designed using a microstrip transmission line integrated with a modified complementary split ring resonator (CSRR). The sensor is optimized to enhance sensitivity while maintaining an operating frequency of approximately 2.4 GHz, making it suitable for integration into future IoT applications. The study examines the impact of resonator placement on sensor performance, utilizing a cost-effective FR-4 substrate. The proposed sensor’s effectiveness is assessed by analyzing the frequency and phase shifts in the transmission coefficient (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>) of glucose solutions compared to pure water, demonstrating its capability to detect subtle changes in glucose concentration. These findings aim to facilitate the development of affordable, reliable, and non-invasive sensors, improving patient comfort and minimizing the risk of infection.

articleTitle: CMOS-Based Memristor Emulator Circuit for Audio Signal Processing in Hearing Aid Applications
abstract: Hearing aids require efficient a nd a daptive audio signal processing to improve sound quality and intelligibility of speech for users. This paper presents the basic building block of an audio processing system using a CMOS-based memristor emulator circuit designed for hearing aid applications. The proposed emulator implemented using SCL 180 nm technology library replicates the behavior of a memristor. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the circuit in building spiking voltage generation similar to that of a biological neuron with minimal power consumption. In this work, the memristive integrate and firing n euron ( MIF) c ell i s d emonstrated i n 180 nm technology, 1.8 V supply voltage, operating frequency upto 100 MHz with a power consumption of less than 1 mW is demonstrated in Cadence Virtuoso tool. Including CMOS-based memristor emulators into hearing aids can lead to significant advancements in adaptive sound processing, ultimately improving the auditory experience for users.

articleTitle: Modelling of Terahertz IMPATT Diodes Based on GaN Using Artificial Neural Networks
abstract: This paper explores the application of artificial neural networks (ANNs) to predict static and dynamic performance metrics of GaN impact avalanche transit time (IMPATT) diodes operating in the terahertz (THz) frequency range. Using datasets derived from self-consistent quantum drift-diffusion (SCQDD) simulations, the ANN models capture key parameters like breakdown voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</inf>), RF power output (PRF), and DC-to-RF conversion efficiency (η<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf>), with significantly reduced computational time. The results show a reduction of computational time by 80%, while achieving accuracy within 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> in prediction errors.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Dual Metal Gate-Split Source and Bilateral Tunnel Field Effect Transistor
abstract: This work introduces a novel Dual Metal Gate-Split Source-Bilateral Tunnel Field-Effect Transistor (DMG-SS-BTFET) designed for ultra-low-power applications. The split-source architecture, integrated with dual-metal gates, enhances the tunneling efficiency and ensures superior electrostatic control over the channel. The proposed DMG-SS-BTFET exhibits significant improvements in I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf>, I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OFF</inf>, SS, and the I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf>/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OFF</inf> ratio compared to conventional TFETs. Its performance is evaluated by comparing the split-source design with a bilateral architecture (DMG-BTFET). Additionally, an RF analysis at a 1 GHz frequency highlights its suitability for high-speed operations. These features position the DMG-SS-BTFET as an advanced candidate for future applications.

articleTitle: Design And Implementation Of Power Efficient Multiplier Using Reversible Logic

authors.preferredName: K S V L D Sai Phanindra
authors.firstName: K S V L D Sai

abstract: In current VLSI Technology, Power Consumption has emerged as a very significant factor to consideration. The primary goal of this project is to design various bits of multiplier using reversible logic circuit with low Power Consumption. Here Power consumption is based on minimum Quantum cost. Lower the Quantum cost lower the Power Consumption. When designing reversible logic algorithms for multipliers, power consumption can be greatly optimized compared to conventional logic-based circuits. Reversible logic is defined by having an equal number of output lines and input lines. Reversible logic includes the use of reversible gates. There are several reversible logic gates, including the Fredkin Gate, Feynman Gate, Double Feynman Gate, Peres Gate, and Toffoli Gate. A comparative study is also given, considering garbage outputs, quantum cost, and the number of gates. Reversible logic is applied in embedded systems where power efficiency is important. In this Project, various bits of multipliers are designed using reversible logic. These circuits are optimized to have minimum quantum cost and produce the least number of garbage outputs.

articleTitle: InAs/Si based Heterojunction TFET as improved in-situ breast cancer biomarker (C-erbB-2) detector
abstract: This work proposes on-site detection of C-erbB-2 biomarker present in saliva/serum using an InAs/Si hetero juncture stacked dielectric Tunnel FET (HJ-SD-TFET). The nanocavities created in the biosensors act as the sensing site for properly detecting antigens. Different concentration ranges (healthy/diseased) of the targeted C-erbB-2 biomarker immobilized in the nanocavities are associated with different interface charge concentrations at the interface of the cavity and underlying gate oxide layer, which affect the device characteristics. The device characteristics are investigated in terms of energy bandgap diagram, electric potential, electric field, carrier concentration and transfer characteristics. Thorough observation of the device characteristics provides vital information regarding the range of C-erbB-2 concentration immobilized in the cavities of the proposed biosensor which serves as detection between healthy and diseased individuals with sufficiently high sensitivity.

articleTitle: Linear Tapered Wavelength Division Multiplexing (WDM) Phasor Array to Improve Coupling Efficiency
abstract: The rapid growth in demand for high-capacity telecommunication links, and the speed limitation of single-wavelength links, has resulted in an extraordinary increase in the use of wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) in advanced lightwave networks. The existing research focuses on waveguide tapering, with limited attention given to tapering effects in WDM phasor arrays. This study introduces a tapered WDM phasor array and investigates how the tapering ratio influences the output field. A WDM phasor array with linear tapering is designed with uniform separation. The performance is analyzed across various tapering ratios and compared with the non-tapered structure. The ouput is analyzed in terms of optical field, electric field and effective refractive index. Results show that lower tapering ratios improve output compared to non-tapered designs, while higher tapering ratios lead to reduced output field strengths.

articleTitle: Corner Pockets in Dual Source Vertical TFET: A Key Strategy for Enhanced DC and RF Performance
abstract: In this work, we introduce a new method focused at improving the performance and execution of Dual Source Vertical Tunnel Field-Effect Transistors (TFETs). A corner source pocket design for the TFET architecture is proposed, which effectively enhances both DC and RF characteristics. By adjusting the geometry of the carrier transport mechanisms, corner pockets increase tunneling efficiency and reduce leakage currents, leading to improvements in subthreshold swing (SS) and on-current (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf>).The proposed structure also shows superior RF performance metrics, namely increased transconductance and reduced parasitic capacitances. The benefits of this novel design are supported by comprehensive simulations and analyses, indicating its potential as a significant advancement for future low-power electronic applications.

articleTitle: Impact of the Threshold Voltage Variability of the Junctionless MOSFET on Digital Performances in Sub-threshold Regime
abstract: The threshold voltage variability of Junctionless MOSFETs (JL-MOSFETs) significantly impacts digital circuit performance, especially in the sub-threshold regime. In this work, we analyze the statistical variations in threshold voltage due to process-induced factors such as channel doping fluctuations, gate work function variations, and oxide thickness non-uniformity. These variations lead to deviations in the sub-threshold swing, on-current (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf>), and off-current (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OFF</inf>), affecting power consumption and switching reliability. Monte Carlo simulations are employed to quantify the impact on key digital performance metrics, including delay, noise margins, and energy efficiency. Results indicate that JL-MOSFETs exhibit lower variability compared to conventional inversion-mode transistors due to their bulk conduction mechanism. However, precise doping control is crucial to minimize degradation in performance. This study highlights the need for optimized device design and variability-aware circuit techniques to enhance JL-MOSFET reliability in ultra-low-power digital applications.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of Tin-Based Perovskite Solar Cell Incorporating 2D Graphene Derivatives as Hole Transport Layer: Optimization of Absorber Layer
abstract: Due to their non-toxic nature and stability, Lead-free tin-based perovskites and inorganic electron transport materials are emerging as a hot research topic in the renewable energy domain. In this work, the effect of the integration of 2-D graphene derivatives as hole transport layer (HTL) in methylammonium tin iodide (MASnI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) based perovskite solar cell (PSC) has been analyzed and the superiority of reduced graphene oxide (rGO) over graphene oxide (GO) has been established using numerical simulation. Different structural parameters of the perovskite absorber layer (PAL) of rGO-based PSC have been optimized to enhance power conversion efficiency (PCE). Other photo voltaic (PV) cell performance metrics like open circuit voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OC</inf>), short circuit current density (J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SC</inf>), and fill factor (FF) have also been studied and analyzed.

articleTitle: Exploring the Analog, RF, and Linearity Performance of Nanosheet FETs under Temperature Variations
abstract: This study investigates the impact of temperature on nanosheet FET performance using a well-established device simulation framework. We analyze DC characteristics, analog/RF figures of merit, and linearity across a range of operating temperatures. While the switching performance degrades at higher temperatures, the drive current increases due to the reduced barrier height. Interestingly, peak transconductance and transition frequency remain largely unaffected by temperature. However, increased output conductance at elevated temperatures leads to a degradation in the maximum oscillation frequency. Conversely, the device’s linearity performance improves with increasing temperature.

articleTitle: Terahertz IMPATTs Based on Wide Band Gap Semiconductor Transit Time Sources
abstract: The probability of wide band gap type-IIb diamond as the foundation for double-drift region (DDR) impact avalanche transit time (IMPATT) devices that operate at THz frequencies has been investigated. In this study, a large-signal (L-S) simulation model is employed. According to simulation studies, the DDR 3C-SiC IMPATTs excel in delivering output power between 140 GHz and 1.0 THz than the diamond IMPATTs. On the other hand, the diamond IMPATT source is a better choice for generating RF power at 94 GHz because it can generate more power at lower millimeter-wave frequencies. At mm-wave and THz frequencies, however, IMPATT sources based on both 3C-SiC and diamond are far more potent than Si IMPATTs. Thereby a co-relative study has been presented for DDR IMPATT based on Si, 3C-SiC, and type-IIb diamond, which shows the superiority of diamond IMPATT, in terms of power and DC to RF conversion efficiency at mm-wave and THz domain.

articleTitle: Enhanced Spin Transfer Torque efficiency in Fe-HfO2/h-BN/Al2O3-Fe compared to existing Fe-MgO-Fe Magnetic Tunnel Junction Device
abstract: Novel MTJs structure comprising of LDMs (MgO, Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, h-BN and HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) as tunnel layer sandwiched between Fe as ferromagnetic (FM) layer is designed for novel magnetic random access memory (MRAM) application. MTJLab Tool with inbuilt non-equilibrium Green’s function (NEGF) model avails in calculating the spin transfer torque (STT) property of MTJs device. As STT define the critical parameters such as switching current density, thermal stability, torque asymmetry and reliability of MTJs. Amongst, HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and h-BN device showed the highest difference in STT components i.e., 1 mA and 0.8 mA along with higher number of stable and accessible memory states. Hence, they are considered as an ideal candidate for implementation as tunnel layer in advance MTJs device.

articleTitle: A Terahertz Narrowband Metamaterial Absorber for Terahertz Sensing Applications
abstract: Metamaterial absorbers have demonstrated significant potential in stealth technologies due to their adaptability and capability to suppress the backscattering of electromagnetic (EM) waves. Developing high-performance absorbers for efficient wave capture and attenuation at terahertz (THz) frequencies remains a complex challenge, requiring innovative material and structural designs. This study presents a THz metamaterial absorber integrating a Zig-Zag-inspired frequency-selective surface (FSS) structure, enhancing absorption efficiency. The proposed -10 dB narrowband absorber at 0.14 THz is fabricated using cost-effective FR<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> and copper materials with a substrate thickness of 1.4 µm. The design achieves near-total absorption (approaching 100%) at a resonant frequency of 4.66 THz, with its absorption characteristics exhibiting high sensitivity to variations in structural parameters due to coupling effects within the zig-zag patterns. Additionally, the frequency-dependent effective permittivity, permeability, and impedance are extracted from reflection data to elucidate the underlying operational principles. The development of metamaterials with near-perfect absorption is essential for applications demanding high absorption efficiency and minimal reflectivity, such as antennas, stealth technologies, and THz sensing.

articleTitle: Development of an IoT-Driven Wireless Smart Health Care System for Continuous Heart Monitoring
abstract: The swift development of IoT driven Telemedicine for the continuous remote monitoring of patients have motivated to use Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) protocol with a Motorized Hand-Cuff type BP Machine, a LoRa enable ESP32 and Raspberry Pi 5 to design an efficient, real time heart monitoring system. The total cardiac health condition was acquired as BP and Heart Rate and transmitted to another location by means of Wireless Communication using a widely used light weight MQTT protocol for our application. The health data was acquired using an affordable and energy efficient LoRa with low-cost sensors and the MQTT protocol was deployed using LoRa and Raspberry pi.

Author Keywords: Motorized Hand Cuff Type BP Machine

articleTitle: Quantum Key Distribution Protocol with Enhanced Eavesdropper Detection Ability
abstract: Quantum key distribution protocols printed a prominent mark in the old path of digital communication by making it even more secure. Unlike its classical counterpart, quantum key distribution protocols exploit the key principles of quantum elements, such as superposition and entanglement, to expose the intrusion in an efficient way. This paper presents a prepare and measure quantum key distribution protocol that detects the eavesdropper more efficiently by inflating bit mismatch between the sender and receiver. The proposed work achieves bit mismatch up to 62.5 percent while Eve is present in the quantum communication channel. The improvement is remarkable in comparison with the classical BB84 protocol, which has a bit mismatch up to 37.5 percent in presence of Eve.

articleTitle: Enhancement of switching current ratio with workfunction modulated SiGe Vertical TFET
abstract: In this work, a new SiGe WFM V-TFET (Workfunction modulated vertical tunnel field effect transistor with SiGe source) is proposed to improve the I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf>/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OFF</inf> ratio and other DC parameters. The study reveals a remarkable rise in transconductance with workfunction modulation, at both the gates. When compared to a conventional Vertical Tunnel Field Effect Transistor (V-TFET), the SiGe WFM V-TFET shows improvements in drain current, surface potential, electric field, energy bandgap, and transconductance. Due to these advancements, this device is allowed to be utilized in high-speed, low-power applications.

articleTitle: Quantum Dots in Photonic and Nano-Optoelectronic Applications
abstract: We theoretically investigate the External-Photoelectric-Effect (EPE) from QDs of opto-electronic nanostructured resources using the k.p. formalism. employing a recently established electron dispersion-law. The photoemitted power varies oscillatorily for every kind of quantum imprisonment for QDs, it is highest and lowest, respectively.

articleTitle: Design of Approximate Multipliers Using Leading Zero/One Detector
abstract: In power-constrained applications like AI, video processing, and embedded systems, energy-efficient hardware is vital. This paper proposes two novel approximate multiplier designs leveraging Leading Zero/One Detector (LZ/OD) circuits implemented on FPGA. Our OptLZOD design introduces an optimized LZ/OD circuit that reduces power consumption by 2.19% compared to LOZD and 41.76% compared to HLR_BM_2. Our R8LZOD design incorporates a radix-8 booth multiplier achieving 1.09%, 37.7%, and 46.2% improvement in Power-Delay Product (PDP) over LOZD, HLR_BM_2, and DURM6_16 respectively. Both designs dynamically adjust bit-width by detecting leading zeros/ones, minimizing energy usage while maintaining acceptable error metrics. These implementations offer compelling solutions for high-speed, low-power applications with minimal performance compromises, demonstrating the efficacy of our approach for energy-efficient hardware design.

articleTitle: Voltage Controlled Gradient as a Mechanism for Skyrmion-Based Racetrack Memory Application on a Synthetic Antiferromagnet Nanotrack
abstract: The magnetic skyrmion is a promising information carrier for next generation logic, neuromorphic computing, and memory devices due to its topological stability, extremely small size, and low operating current. A computational demonstration of a skyrmion driven on a synthetic antiferromagnet nanotrack using a voltage controlled magnetic anisotropy gradient for the application of racetrack memory device is studied in this work. The velocity of the skyrmion is dependent on Gilbert damping constant. The proposed device makes use of the notch at the end of the nanotrack ensuring a constant flow of ‘0’ and ‘1’ bits without any accumulation on the racetrack.

articleTitle: Detection of Brain Tumor using Convolution Neural Network through Detection of Metastasis
abstract: A novel model using convolution neural network has been developed for near accurate detection of brain tumor by carefully preprocessing the data and addressing class imbalance. Dataset was gathered between December 2017 and March 2018, consists of 7,001 JPG MRI pictures, 3,800 of which show a healthy brain, and 3,201 of which show a brain with tumors; results 94.14% accuracy in training, 94.33% accuracy in testing and 95.12% accuracy in validation. Insignificant losses are reported in all the cases, speaks in favor of quality of segregation between pathological and normal tissues. Present study provides 92.39% sensitivity, 96.63% specificity and 97.03% precision which clearly outperforms peer-reviewed works carried out using CNN; and therefore, justifies novelty of the work.

articleTitle: Impact of Cap Layer Engineering on the DC and RF Performance of N-Polar AlGaN/GaN HEMTs
abstract: In this work, we investigated the impact of cap layer engineering on the N-polar AlGaN/GaN HEMTs. By varying the drain side n+ GaN cap layer length (L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cap</inf>) from 150 nm to 350 nm, we analyze its effects on the key DC and RF performance parameters, including transconductance (g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>), on-resistance (R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf>), cut-off frequency (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf>), and the on-state to off-state current ratio (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf>/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OFF</inf> ). The results indicates that increasing L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cap</inf> enhanced the drain current, reduced the R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf>, and improved the f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf>. The DC measurements shows a maximum drain current of 1.02 mA/μm at a gate-source voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GS</inf>) of 2 V, a maximum g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf> of 0.81 mS/μm at drain-source voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DS</inf>) of 5 V for L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cap</inf> = 350 nm. A peak f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf> of 68.7 GHz was measured at a V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DS</inf> of 5 V for L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cap</inf> = 350 nm. These findings emphasizes the significant role of cap layer optimization in enhancing the electrostatic and transport properties of N-polar HEMTs, making them promising candidates for high-frequency and high-power applications.

articleTitle: Parametric Optimization of Verilog-A code for Double-PHL of RRAM Device in a Step-by-Step Approach
abstract: The requirement of precise mathematical modeling and corresponding Verilog-A implementation is pivotal for circuit designing of many applications, like, non-volatile memory, logic circuits, and neuromorphic computing, with memristor devices, possessing pinched hysteresis loop (PHL) in I-V characteristics. A few works were reported with single PHL behavior; but yet to correlate with multilevel PHL, as aligned with experimental reports. The present work focuses on the development of such a model by optimization in the parametric level in the Simmons model, well adopted to describe single PHL conventionally, step-by-step, alteration of parameters and comparison with experimental data is the key methodology of this work. Proposing threshold voltage, as a new parameter, is substantial for appreciable agreement for simultaneous matching of the double loop (PHL) case. The matching shows an appreciable error of ~7% for lower–voltage PHL and that of ~3% for higher-voltage PHL.

articleTitle: Leveraging FPGA for k-Nearest Neighbours Classifier: Design and Performance Study
abstract: In the era of big data, real-time processing and fast decision-making are essential. The k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN) algorithm, though effective, becomes computationally expensive on traditional CPUs, especially with large or high-dimensional datasets. Implementing k-NN on Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) offers a solution by leveraging parallel processing for accelerated computation. This work presents an in-depth analysis of FPGA-based k-NN implementation using HDL, comparing its performance with CPUs and GPUs. The results demonstrate significant improvements in speed and efficiency, highlighting the potential of FPGA-based acceleration in machine learning applications. This approach paves the way for scalable, high-performance classification in domains such as healthcare, finance, and e-commerce.

articleTitle: High Speed 16T DPTL Full Adder with Reduced Power Dissipation
abstract: This paper presents the design of a high-speed, low-noise Full Adder with reduced power dissipation using Differential Pass Transistor Logic (DPTL), which can be optimized for the integration into an n x n-bit multiplier. The proposed full adder circuit addresses critical requirements for high-speed operation, reduced power dissipation making it suitable for modern-generation digital systems where energy efficiency and high-speed arithmetic processing are essential. Differential Pass Transistor Logic (DPTL), as opposed to conventional CMOS logic, provides notable improvements in power, speed, and area, especially by leveraging NMOS-only configurations. These enhancements make DPTL a promising choice for arithmetic units in ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) and MAC (Multiply-Accumulate) operations. The proposed low time delay 16T DPTL Full Adder was designed in LTspiceXVII with CMOS 180nm bulk Technology. The proposed Full Adder has an Average Delay of 3.33 ns and a power dissipation of 5.32µW. The speed of the Full Adder is enhanced by 61% and the power dissipation is reduced by 25% compared to the existing design.

articleTitle: High-K, Gate-Stack Engineered, Junctionless, Nanowire Ferroelectric Field Effect Transistor (J-NW-Fe-Fet) with various catalytic metals for PH3 Sensing Applications
abstract: In order to detect phosphine (PH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) gas, this script proposed a Junctionless-Nanowire-Ferroelectric Field Effect Transistor (J-NW-Fe-Fet) to detect phosphine gas for low-power and high sensitive based applications. In order to lower the sub-threshold swing below 60 mV/decade, the ferroelectric layer of Si:HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> has been employed as a stack, based on the negative capacitance phenomena. Furthermore, three catalytic metals- Chromium (Cr), Iridium (Ir), and Rhodium (Rh) as gate electrodes have been employed to build the J-NW-Fe-Fet as a phosphine gas sensor. Several electrical characteristics, such as potential and electron concentration, have been investigated in the design of the PH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> gas sensor. Additionally, variations in drain-current (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ds</inf>), trans-conductance (g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>), and output-conductance (g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf>), are simulated for various catalytic metals at different channel lengths (L= 30 nm, 40 nm & 50 nm) at the gate electrode in order to evaluate the sensor's performance. The ATLAS 3-D simulator has been used to carry out the simulations.

articleTitle: Single and Multiple Fault Detection in Analog Circuits Using V-Transform Coefficients
abstract: This paper introduces a novel method for detecting soft faults in linear and non-linear analog circuits. The proposed technique, V-Transform coefficient (VTC) testing, is an extension of existing coefficient-based methodologies. The proposed method effectively identifies various fault conditions by analyzing the V-Transform coefficients of the circuit's output. Extensive simulations were conducted using SPICE to validate the proposed method, injecting various faults into elliptic and leapfrog filters. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of V-Transform coefficient testing in accurately detecting both single and multiple faults. Our findings highlight the potential of this approach for improving the reliability and fault tolerance of analog circuits.

articleTitle: 8-Bit Approximate Multiplier using Approximate Full Adder
abstract: Approximate computing has gained significant attention in recent years due to its ability to trade computational accuracy for improvements in power, area, and speed. This paper presents three novel approximate full adders used in the Wallace multiplier, aimed at error-resilient applications such as image processing and machine learning. The proposed designs are evaluated for key performance metrics, including power consumption and error rate, using hardware simulations. Comparative analysis with existing approximate multipliers demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed design in achieving a balance between accuracy and hardware efficiency. This work exhibits improved accuracy with a Mean Error Distance (MED) of 30.62 in all the proposed designs, compared to previous low power design (EAFA2) with an MED of approximately 156.17. Additionally, DAFA3 achieves a 41% power reduction compared to an exact full adder.

articleTitle: Development of Optimised Maximum Power Point Tracking Controller for Solar Photo-Voltaic Power Conversion System
abstract: This paper focuses on the development of optimised maximum power point tracking (MPPT) process for solar photo-voltaic (PV) and DC-DC boost converter-based energy conversion scheme. The method is more effective under multiple peaks of power-voltage characteristics of PV module, as the conventional MPPT fails to track the global peak of power. In this regard, Cuckoo Search (CS) based MPPT method is developed in software platform. The method exhibits higher efficiency for tracking the global peak than the conventional Perturb and Observe (P&O) MPPT technique. Furthermore, the hardware implementation of Cuckoo Search (CS) based MPPT method for production of switching pulses using the microcontroller (NucleoG474RE) is done, which is useful to drive the power converter in practice.

articleTitle: Efficient Error Detection and Correction code based on Improved Redundant Matrix Code (IRMC) Algorithm
abstract: Mobile way communication over the Internet requires error detection and correction. The detection of error at the data link layer can be controlled by network handling techniques. Data traffic, signaling and control will be carried out by two channels of network connection. Error detection will be done for traffic channels of the information bits, encoded correction code together forms the transmitted data stream. Currently, the error is tolerated by the SRAM memory frame, so Single Cell Upsets (SCU) or Multiple Cell Upsets (MCU) can occur. One of the main reasons for the MCU is astronomical radiation.
