The proposed technique is called Improved Redundant Matrix Code (IRMC) to protect memories from the detuning of many components, is used to detect and troubleshoot storage devices. IRMC's detection rate and adjustments contrast with other rescue codes. Space, power, and defer overhead is only. Results should prove that IRMC has higher quality and higher correctability for MCU tuned for the lower power and delay. Xlinx 14.7 is the tool used for the process and using Verilog HDL, programming of the algorithm is performed.

articleTitle: Design of Low Power and High Speed CAM-assisted 9T SRAM cell on 14nm FinFET Technology
abstract: One of the key considerations in the design of low power Very-large-scale integration (VLSI) circuits is leakage power dissipation, which is entirely responsible for the circuit's overall performance. Because of the leakage and power consumption, the battery's long-lasting components lose their functionality quickly and reduce the system performance. So, in this research, the Fin-shaped Field-Effect Transistor (FinFET) based 9T SRAM cell is intended for achieving low power consumption and leakage current to speed up the write operations with the Content Addressable Memory(CAM)-assisted circuit. Moreover, the Reconfigurable Sense Amplifier (RSA) is designed to optimize the speed of memory operations, thus improving the whole performance of the SRAM circuit. In the end, a Tanner EDA tool is used to execute the proposed CAM-assisted 9T SRAM design. The performance outcomes show that the proposed design yields 10 μA leakage current, which is comparatively smaller than the existing designs.

Author Keywords: high speed read and write operations

articleTitle: Crosstalk in Quantum Cellular Automata Networks
abstract: Quantum Cellular Automata (QCA) is a promising computational paradigm leveraging quantum mechanics for high-speed data processing with minimal power consumption. QCA circuits use quantum cells to encode and transmit data via Coulombic interactions between adjacent cells. Crosstalk in QCA networks refers to unintended interference between quantum states of neighboring cells, potentially degrading processing speed and accuracy in computations and data transfer. This study examines the nature, causes, and performance impacts of crosstalk, along with various mitigation strategies. Observations reveal varying power consumption due to errors in identical logic circuits, enabling optimal circuit selection. Future research directions focus on minimizing crosstalk and improving QCA reliability for low-power devices and quantum computing applications.

articleTitle: High-Performance Accelerator for Post-Quantum Cryptography Using Crystals Dilithium with Area Optimization
abstract: The rise of quantum-capable adversaries has driven global efforts to standardize post-quantum cryptographic primitives. Once standardized, existing security protocols must efficiently integrate these schemes. This work presents an optimized implementation of CRYSTALS-Dilithium, NIST’s chosen post-quantum digital signature scheme. By leveraging parallelism, pre-computation, and efficient memory management, we achieve a compact design suitable for small Zynq FPGA devices. On the Zynq Ultrascale+ platform, our approach improves the Area×Time trade-off for KeyGen, Sign, and Verify by 36.7%, 35.4%, and 42.3%, respectively. Additionally, it reduces bit complexity by up to 91.2% and storage by 72.5% for signature generation at various security levels compared to conventional NTT-based methods.

articleTitle: A 2.5 W Class-F Power Amplifier using Balanced Stub Harmonics on 150 nm GaN HEMT device for 5G Applications
abstract: This letter proposes a novel MMIC Class-F power amplifier (PA) designed on 150 nm GaN process for 5G front end. Class-F amplification is achieved by controlling harmonics of output power through balanced stub arrangement thus switching current and voltage at output node. The designed amplifier provides linear gain greater than 15 dB, 2 W output power with 34.2% power added efficiency (PAE) for 26 GHz band of 5G operation. The circuit is designed for two stage amplification with Chebyshev low pass filter as output matching network (OMN) using L-type topology and balanced stub technique, for suppressing harmonics thus generating class-F amplifier. Additionally, a low-Q L-type input matching network and two stage L-type biasing network are used for reducing circuit complexity and for improving circuit performance. The designed amplifier is reducing complexity issues of class-F as well as providing better performance due to ability of nanoscale devices.

articleTitle: Enhancing the RF/Analog Performance of a Germanium Source Double Gate Ferroelectric Tunnel FET by the Gate Stack Modification Using Different Ferroelectric Materials
abstract: Ferroelectric tunnel field effect transistors are well known for their lower supply voltage operation and improved electrostatic characteristics in low power IoT applications. In this article we performed a systematic 2-D Silvaco TCAD simulation based comparative analysis of several RF/Analog parameters of a germanium source double gate ferroelectric tunnel FET using various well known ferroelectric materials on the gate stack of the proposed device. Germanium source form heterojunction with silicon channel at the source channel interface and a heterojunction ferroelectric tunnel FETs may achieve a steep subthreshold swing of 26.7 mV/decade with essentially no ambipolar conduction and a significant increase in ON current when compared to conventional TFETs due to the combined effect of band to band tunneling and negative capacitance. Scaling the ferroelectric layer thickness below its critical thickness can reduce hysteretic losses by stabilizing the negative capacitance effect for ferroelectric polarization. This is ideal for high frequency switching and ultra-low power applications.

articleTitle: Compact Dual-Port MIMO Microstrip Patch Antenna for Terahertz Applications in 6G Communications
abstract: This study introduces a dual-port MIMO antenna featuring a two-element microstrip patch array, specifically designed for THz applications with an emphasis on 6G communication systems. Developed on an FR-4 substrate with copper elements, the antenna achieves notable miniaturization, with dimensions of 52 × 48.5 µm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and a thickness of 1.6 µm. By incorporating an H-shaped slot and strategic notches, the patch size is reduced by 51%. The proposed design exhibits a primary resonant frequency at 2.71 THz, with secondary resonances at 4.3 THz and 5.7 THz, achieving return loss values of 40.40 dB and approximately -30 dB, respectively. The antenna demonstrates a gain of 3.15 dBi, linear polarization, and high directivity. Simulations conducted in CST Microwave Studio validate the antenna’s high performance, including a broad operational bandwidth of 4.69 THz covering the range from 2.22 THz to 6.91 THz, excellent impedance matching with a VSWR of 1.01, and an efficiency of 61%. The dual port MIMO configuration ensures minimal mutual coupling, evidenced by a low ECC of 3.26 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−5</sup> and a reduced CCL including the isolation of 25 dB. These results confirm the antenna’s suitability for advanced applications such as terahertz communications, high-speed data transfer, and sensing systems, offering an optimal combination of compactness, efficiency, and reliability.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Dual-Element Microstrip Patch Antenna Array for Multi-Band 6G Terahertz Applications
abstract: The research introduces a miniaturized, high-performance rectangular microstrip patch antenna array specifically engineered for 6G applications. The proposed design features a two-element microstrip array constructed from copper on a 1.6 μm FR-4 substrate, capable of operating at three significant resonant frequencies within the 2-11 THz range: 2.9 THz, 7.56 THz, and 10.23 THz. With a compact footprint of 30 × 48 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, the design achieves a 51% reduction in patch size, making it highly suitable for space-constrained environments while maintaining optimal efficiency. The implementation of strategically placed slots and notches yields return loss values of -24.92 dB, -32.06 dB, and -24.89 dB at the respective frequencies, alongside directive gains of 5.67 dBi, 7.49 dBi, and 8.27 dBi, thereby ensuring robust power transmission. Furthermore, the incorporation of an "H"-shaped slot, and notches contribute to the stability of operational parameters, enhancing the antenna's reliability. This multi-band antenna is optimized for the 1-10 THz frequency range, facilitating a range of applications, including ultra-fast 6G communication, security scanning, space exploration, environmental sensing, and high-speed on-chip data transfer. The findings underscore the significant potential of this antenna design for next-generation communication technologies and advanced applications.

articleTitle: IoT and Cloud-Based Automated Saline Fluid Control System for Intravenous Therapy
abstract: Intravenous (IV) therapy is a vital medical procedure for managing fluid levels and delivering medications directly into the bloodstream. However, traditional IV systems rely heavily on continuous manual monitoring, leading to inefficiencies and a higher risk of human error, particularly in resource-limited healthcare settings. This paper presents an innovative IoT-enabled automated saline fluid control system aimed at improving patient care and reducing the workload on medical staff. The system integrates advanced sensors, a NodeMCU microcontroller, and cloud-based data storage via ThingSpeak to enable real-time monitoring and precise control of saline levels. A servo motor is used to automatically stop the saline flow when critical thresholds are reached, preventing complications such as reverse blood flow and air embolisms. By combining automation, remote monitoring, and data-driven analytics, this solution enhances the safety and efficiency of IV therapy. It minimizes the need for human intervention, offers valuable insights to healthcare providers, and provides a cost-effective, scalable alternative for hospitals and clinics globally.

articleTitle: An Improved IIR Filter Design using Artificial Rabbits Optimization Algorithm and its FPGA Implementation
abstract: This paper presents a meta-heuristic optimization algorithm known as Artificial Rabbits Optimization (ARO) to get the optimal set of infinite impulse response (IIR) filter coefficients. Application of the ARO algorithm to design two real-life examples is used for performance testing. The proposed algorithm is simulated to get the coefficients of different types of linear and non-linear (with noise and without noise) problems with similar order and lower order, and the simulated results are compared with few recent optimization algorithms such as Salp Swarm Algorithm (SSA), Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA), and Dragonfly Algorithm (DA). The proposed algorithm is much faster and efficient than the numerous standard algorithms. The Proposed ARO algorithm demonstrates a lower Mean Square Error (MSE) and superior convergence speed as compared to the other optimization techniques examined herein. FPGA implementation is performed to design IIR filters where ARO shows better performance.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Algorithms for Enhancing Stroke Prediction in Healthcare Database
abstract: Stroke is a major global cause of disability and death, often resulting from sudden blockages in the brain or heart. Recognizing early warning signs can help reduce stroke risk and is crucial for effective stroke prevention and management. This study enhances stroke prediction using machine learning and neural networks, analyzing risk factors like hypertension, heart disease, ever-married, work type, residence type, glucose levels, BMI, smoking, gender, and age. Ten machine learning algorithms are tested on a well-curated clinical dataset. The results showed high accuracy for Random Forest (98.17%), Logistic Regression (98.32%), CatBoost (98.52%), and an Ensemble Technique (98.63%). However, the Artificial Neural Network (ANN) outperformed all with 99.37% accuracy, the highest AUC score, and the lowest false positive rate. These findings highlight ANN’s effectiveness in stroke risk assessment, offering valuable insights for improved prevention and timely medical interventions.

Index Terms: Reduction In The Risk Of Stroke

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Differential Amplifiers Using Cadence with GPDK45, GPDK90, and GPDK180
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of differential amplifier circuits designed using three process technologies: GPDK45, GPDK90, and GPDK180. Utilizing Cadence design and simulation tools, we perform detailed simulations to evaluate and compare key performance parameters of these architectures. The analysis focuses on critical metrics such as propagation delay, gain, power consumption, and bandwidth, which play a pivotal role in determining the overall efficiency and suitability of differential amplifiers for various applications. The simulation results highlight the impact of technology scaling on the performance characteristics, offering insights into trade-offs and optimization strategies. By systematically comparing the outputs across these process nodes, the study provides valuable guidelines for the selection of process technology based on specific design requirements and application domains.

articleTitle: Junctionless Spacer-Engineered SOI FinFET-Based Hydrogen Gas Sensor: Electrical Characterization and Sensitivity Analysis
abstract: This research presents a novel junctionless spacer-engineered gate stacked Silicon-On-Insulator (SOI) FinFET for hydrogen gas sensing. The study investigates the sensor’s transfer characteristics, energy band diagram and surface potential under varying pressures. Threshold voltage and switching ratio sensitivities are calculated to assess the sensor’s responsiveness. A maximum value of 125.64 for I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf>/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OFF</inf> sensitivity and 0.24 for V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TH</inf> sensitivity is obtained at P=10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-10</sup> Torr. Simulations performed on 3D ATLAS Silvaco tool reveal significant differences in performance between the junctionless (JLT) sensor and the one having a junction. Specifically, the JLT fin-based sensor demonstrates substantially improved sensitivity to hydrogen gas. The combination of improved sensitivity and the SOI FinFET architecture presents a promising approach for designing high-performance hydrogen gas sensors suitable for diverse applications using JLT SOI FinFETs.

articleTitle: Low-Noise Amplifier Design and S-Parameter Analysis in Advanced CMOS Technologies for Modern Communication Systems
abstract: The LNA is an integral block of RF and communication systems for amplification of low-level signals with minimum noise such that the SNR is within acceptable limits. This work presents the cascode LNA design with inductive degeneration optimized and analyzed for state-of-the-art communication systems with innovative circuit-level modifications to improve noise performance and linearity, responding to the specific requirements of next-generation wireless devices. The LNA is implemented and analyzed in Cadence Virtuoso using the 45nm CMOS technology node for performance enhancements over conventional designs. Among the important modifications are inductive degeneration optimization; it involves tuning the inductor values for a compromise between noise suppression and gain bandwidth. Other modifications include active biasing to stabilize the operating point, keeping the amplifier in the linear region, providing improved performance, and reduced distortion. The S-parameters are analyzed through simulation, involving frequency response, gain compression (1 dB point), impedance matching, and stability analysis. The simulation results indicate gains in excess of -20 dB, less than -15 dB, some impressive noise performance, and representing viable device performance levels for the current communication systems. Thus, the proposed design versus the tunable LNA model and CMOS low-noise amplifier with source degeneration model proves that it serves a higher performance level-ranged design with less noise figure, improved linearity, and stability for a wireless communication device next.

articleTitle: Parametric Evaluation of MOSFET based Biosensor Accounting Non-Ideal Hybridization Dynamics
abstract: This article tries to analytically investigate the architecture of a Label free Dielectric Modulated Triple Material Stacked Surrounding Gate Junctionless Metal Oxide Semiconductor Field Effect Transistor (DMTMSSGJL-MOSFET) based Biosensor by incorporating various non-ideal conditions like steric hindrance issues so as to realize and embrace the practicality of the model. For structural formation, a stacked surrounding gate-oxide alongside with the employment of gate work-function engineering and a symmetrical junctionless doping profile is deployed for the proposed device. The thought process behind this article is to develop quantitative formulation of various non-ideal issues in association with steric hindrance problem and to measure the underlying biometric performance parameter of the device in terms of threshold voltage sensitivity (SVTH) for both charged and neutral biomolecules. Furthermore, a comprehensive analysis of different non-uniform patterns of biomolecules inside the nanogap cavities are analyzed to replicate the reduced interaction likelihood of various biomolecules.

articleTitle: Modulation of Electro-Chemical Sensing Properties in MoSe2 Nanosheet towards CO Detection via Incorporating Foreign Platinum Atom
abstract: The current study investigates the electronic and chemo-sensing properties of a pristine 2D molybdenum diselenide (MoSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) nanosheet and a platinum (Pt)-doped MoSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanosheet, concerning their ability in adsorbing toxic carbon monoxide (CO) gas. First principle-based calculations were performed to analyze the adsorption characteristics of CO on pristine MoSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> (System I) and Pt-doped MoSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> (System II), using the Gaussian 09W and GaussView 6.0 software packages. Various electronic properties, including the Highest Occupied Molecular Orbital (HOMO), Lowest Unoccupied Molecular Orbital (LUMO), Electrostatic Potential (ESP), and Electron Localization Function (ELF), were examined, to elucidate the atomic-level interactions between CO and the two considered nanosheets. To visualize the electron localization/delocalization present within the molecular and atomic structure, ELF mapping was employed. The molecular structures of both systems were analyzed using infrared (IR) spectroscopy. Calculations revealed that CO exhibited stronger interaction with the pristine MoSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanosheet compared to the Pt-decorated one, as indicated by a higher negative value (in magnitude) of adsorption energy (-1.98 eV) for System-I. For both the systems recovery time (in seconds) and electronic conductivity, were measured. FTIR and Raman spectroscopy were plotted for CO adsorbed Pt-doped MoSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanosheet to analyze the results with experimental verification. The findings inferred that Pt cannot be considered as a suitable dopant for enhancing CO detection in MoSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanosheets.

articleTitle: Floating Point Multipliers on FPGAs
abstract: This work presents IEEE 754 compliant floatingpoint multipliers for various formats: Half Precision (HP), Single Precision (SP), Double Precision (DP), Double Extended Precision (DEP), and Quadruple Precision (QP), with bit lengths of 16, 32, 64, 80, and 128 bits, respectively, implemented on Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs). The study explores different mantissa multipliers – Optimized Schoolbook Multiplier (OBSM), Hybrid Karatsuba Multiplier (HKM) and Hybrid Recursive Karatsuba Multiplier (HRKM) – to identify the most efficient mantissa multipliers that comply with the IEEE 754 standard and are suitable for floating-point multipliers. Hardware implementations show that the proposed HRKM-based SP and DP floating-point multipliers show a better Area-Time-Product (ATP) performance of 79. 599% and 83. 901%, respectively, in comparison to the latest state-of-the-art work on the AMD Kintex Ultrascale KCU105 FPGA platform.

articleTitle: Modified Adaptive Kalman Filtering with Multiple Fading Factors in 2-D Land Vehicle Navigation
abstract: Extended Kalman Filtering (EKF) and its modified techniques have been used worldwide for various vehicle navigation tasks. Several adaptive algorithms have been presented to overcome the issue of inaccurate a priori knowledge of the statistical noise of the system and measurement models in EKF. Among them, Single Fading factor Adaptive Kalman filter (SFAKF) and Multiple Fading factor Adaptive Kalman Filtering (MFAKF) techniques introduce the concept of fading factors to significantly reduce the influence of these abnormalities on the state estimation. This research work first demonstrates a successful implementation of SFAKF and MFAKF algorithms in 2-D land vehicle navigation. Then, a Modified Multiple Fading factor Adaptive Kalman Filtering (MMFAKF) algorithm has also been proposed which has modified the fading factor function to produce superior results over other competing algorithms, thus increasing reliability on estimation using real time data acquired from GNSS/ INS systems.

Author Keywords: Single Fading Factor Adaptive Kalman Filter (SFAKF)
Multiple Fading Factor Adaptive Kalman filter (MFAKF)
Modified Multiple Fading Factor Adaptive Kalman filter (MMFAKF)

articleTitle: Detection of Diabetic Retinopathy Using Machine Learning: A Comprehensive Review
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a leading cause of vision loss and blindness, particularly among diabetic individuals. Early detection is vital to prevent severe complications, yet manual screening remains labor-intensive and error-prone. This study reviews advancements in DR detection through machine learning (ML), focusing on support vector machines (SVM), convolutional neural networks (CNN), and deep learning frame-works. Examining research from the past decade, we explore methodologies, datasets, and feature extraction techniques for automated DR identification. A comparative evaluation highlights model strengths, limitations, and potential enhancements. Our objective is to advance ML-based diagnostic tools for clinical implementation, improving efficiency and accuracy in DR screening. Ultimately, this can enhance patient outcomes and reduce blindness risks, contributing to more effective diabetic retinopathy management.

articleTitle: Lightweight 64-bit AES-Inspired Symmetric Cryptographic Core for Low-Power and Resource-Constrained Systems
abstract: The paper presents the design of a lightweight, high-speed and low-power symmetric cryptographic core inspired by the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) for resource-constrained environments like IoT applications and embedded systems. The proposed architecture retains AES principles while optimizing for minimal resource utilization by reducing block and key sizes to 64 bits. The design is implemented using SystemVerilog, synthesized and simulated on Xilinx Kintex-7 (xc7k70t-fbv676) FPGA to evaluate performance metrics. The simulation results verify the correctness of encryption and decryption operations, and timing analysis indicates encryption and decryption latencies of 70 ns and 75 ns, respectively. The core runs at an optimized frequency of 228.65 MHz and processes at a throughput of 248.02 Mbps, which is appropriate for real-time secure communication. The low hardware footprint, optimized combinational logic, and minimal switching activity contribute to significantly reduced dynamic power consumption, making this cryptographic core a low-power alternative for security applications.

articleTitle: Investigation of FinFET in terms of Device Design, Performance, and its Challenges
abstract: The paper provides an overview of the historical background, formation process, and operational mechanisms of FinFET. Overcoming the challenge of dimension scaling has been a consistent effort to fulfill the requirements of high-performance, high-density, low-power, and low-voltage intricate devices. Miniaturization serves as the primary catalyst for transitioning from microelectronic to nanoelectronic device structures. Planar CMOS scaling has consistently delivered improved performance and low-power devices at the forefront of technology nodes for more than three decades. The discussion also includes a review of various types of FinFETs, exploring diverse structures and materials to enhance performance. The paper delves into challenges encountered in FinFET development, such as corner effects (fin shape), parasitic capacitance and resistance, and fin patterning. Looking forward, a potential avenue to maximize FinFET's potential involves fostering the development and application of Gate-All-Around FETs (GAAFETs) based on FinFET technology.

articleTitle: Covariance Matrix-Based DOA Estimation Using CNN: Performance Across Narrow and Wide Grids
abstract: Deep learning has emerged as a powerful tool for enhancing Direction-of-Arrival (DOA) estimation, offering resilience to noise, model mismatches, and computational inefficiencies inherent in traditional methods. This paper proposes a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based approach that leverages covariance matrices of received signals to extract spatial features critical for precise DOA estimation. The proposed model demonstrates robust performance across narrow and wide angular grids under varying Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) conditions. Notably, it achieves a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) below 3.5 degrees for the narrow grid and within 24 degrees for the wide grid, even at SNR levels as low as -20 dB. The study highlights the model’s ability to generalize effectively while acknowledging performance gaps for extreme noise and broader angular separations. A comparative analysis with traditional methods underscores the computational efficiency and adaptability of the CNN framework. Future work will focus on hybrid models, real-world dataset expansion, and architectural optimizations to enhance scalability in next-generation sensing and communication applications.

articleTitle: Memristor Synaptic Array with Spiking Neurons for Neuromorphic Audio Signal Recognition
abstract: After successful realization of memristor by HP, it has gained momentum for realization of neuromorphic circuits and systems, since it demonstrates a similar characteristic of biological neural systems. In this work, audio signal processing with a spiking neural network architecture using the memristor as the memory element has been realized. This paper implements an integrated computer-in-memory architecture that uses a memristor crossbar array to reduce latency bandwidth using vector-matrix multiplication. With minimum latency the architecture identifies the new feed audio signal from the mixture of stored signals. Further, a TTFS (Time to First Spike) encoding scheme is realized using an LIF neuron for generating a spike train for enhancing the digitization of input audio signals, and in the output stage, it classifies the voltage levels for audio enhancement. The proposed design achieves 98% accuracy, consuming 0.676mW of power and 22pJ per synapse during audio signal processing.

articleTitle: PV Based Smart Villages for Sustainable Living in Coastal Region of West Bengal
abstract: Solar panels are essential for harnessing solar energy. However, a single panel cannot generate a significant amount of power unless combined in parallel or series configurations, which can be space-consuming. By increasing the number of solar panels, we can meet the growing demand for electricity. To maintain the power system's functionality, it is necessary to connect individual batteries in both series and parallel arrangements, ensuring appropriate voltage and electric flow levels. Proper inverter ratings are also important. Safety is paramount, requiring the installation of rated fuses and sufficient component isolation. Since batteries and inverters generate heat during operation, they must be placed in well-ventilated areas. Solar panels should be installed in locations situated coastal area of West Bengal named G-Plot under the Pathar Pratima Block of extended part of Sundarban with ample sunlight.

articleTitle: Computational Intelligence Approach of IoT in Real Time Smart Agriculture Monitoring
abstract: The implementation of the Internet of Things (IoT) into agriculture is rooted in traditional farming practices and based on modern technologies, which allows to achieve an all-new level enhancement productivity, increased resource efficiency conquering sustainability. With the help of this study author investigates the utilization of IoT in agriculture and elaborates on how a network of devices simply collects, processes all real-time input like soil health, weather conditions, crop growth etc. Enabled by the Internet of Things, precision agriculture will fine tune field-by-field management to optimize irrigation water use and fertilizer application and reduce pest control. It is soil moisture sensors with automated irrigation systems that deliver just the right amount of water, thus saving valuable resources and ensuring optimal crop hydration. Drones carry multispectral sensors that can quickly assess crop health and identify pest outbreaks so locally-focused solutions are used, minimizing chemical use with optimal results. IoT can also create new methods of managing the health and behavior of livestock, increasing herd productivity as well as disease management. In addition, IoT enables farm to fork supply traceability contributing towards the food safety and quality. Although there are major advantages, hurdles including increased upfront costs, security concerns and limited rural Internet connections remain to dampen enthusiasm. This subject indicates some evidence relating to the use of IoT in smart agriculture explaining its significant approach for sustainable, efficient and productive farming practices.

articleTitle: Multi-Modal Fusion of Spatial and Temporal Features for Radar Signal Sensing
abstract: Communication and radar signal sensing are pivotal for modern wireless and intelligent sensing systems. Traditional techniques, including feature-engineered methods and standalone neural networks, often struggle to handle multi-modal data effectively and perform poorly in low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) environments. These approaches fail to capture spatial and temporal dependencies and lack mechanisms for leveraging inter-modal relationships. A CNN-LSTM-Based Attention-Augmented Multi-Feature Fusion Network has been proposed to overcome these challenges. This architecture utilizes convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for spatial feature extraction, long short-term memory (LSTM) networks for modelling temporal dependencies, and an attention mechanism to refine features across modalities dynamically. The model ensures robust signal sensing under challenging conditions by integrating IQ data, spectrograms, and cyclic spectrum representations. Extensive experiments validate the proposed method's superiority, achieving over 99.7% sensing accuracy over Gaussian and racian channel. The network demonstrates strong resilience in SNRs as low as -5 dB, outperforming traditional methods. Performance metrics and experimental results confirm its effectiveness and emphasize its potential as a robust framework for advancing communication and radar signal sensing.

articleTitle: Advancements in Li-Ion Battery Materials for Battery Energy Storage Systems
abstract: Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) play a crucial role in modern energy systems, driven by the increasing demand for grid stabilization, electric vehicles (EVs), and renewable energy integration. This review examines the materials and technologies supporting BESS, with a particular focus on Lithium-Ion (Li-Ion) batteries, their alternatives, and future prospects. Li-Ion batteries remain the dominant technology due to their high energy density and efficiency; however, they face challenges such as material scarcity, safety concerns, and energy limitations. Finally, key challenges and research opportunities in advancing BESS technology are discussed, emphasizing the need for higher energy densities, improved safety, and economic feasibility for large-scale energy storage solutions.

articleTitle: Hybrid and Ensemble Machine Learning Models for Effective Imbalanced Data Classification
abstract: This study explores the effectiveness of advanced machine learning models in addressing classification challenges within imbalanced datasets. In this paper, two models are developed, specifically Support Vector Machine (SVM) with Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) and Autoencoder + Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), while two models, Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) and XGBoost, are implemented for comparison.These models are evaluated using robust metrics such as Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC), Balanced Accuracy, and Receiver Operating Characteristic Area Under the Curve (ROC AUC) Score to ensure a comprehensive assessment. The results reveal the exceptional performance of the developed hybrid models, with the SVM with MLP model emerging as the most reliable due to its strong balance between precision and recall. The Autoencoder + XGBoost model closely follows, excelling in handling imbalanced data and delivering consistent results. Among the implemented models, LightGBM showcases robust classification capabilities, offering a scalable and effective alternative, while XGBoost, although reliable, demonstrates limitations in handling complex class distributions compared to the developed approaches. This analysis underscores the importance of leveraging hybrid architectures for achieving high-performance classification in data-intensive and imbalanced scenarios. By combining feature extraction and advanced classification techniques, these models not only improve predictive accuracy but also ensure better handling of class imbalance.

articleTitle: Optimized Rectenna Design for Wireless Power Transfer in Implantable Systems
abstract: The integration of radio frequency (RF)-based wireless power transfer (WPT) systems into implantable medical devices (IMDs) represents a transformative step toward realizing fully autonomous, battery-free biomedical implants. This study presents the design, simulation, and optimization of a miniaturized implantable rectenna operating at the 2.4 GHz ISM band, aimed at addressing the critical challenges of power delivery, biocompatibility, and electromagnetic safety. A multi-layered human tissue phantom model incorporating realistic dielectric properties is developed to assess in-situ antenna performance and ensure compliance with specific absorption rate (SAR) regulations. The antenna is geometrically optimized for low return loss, minimal volume, and efficient power harvesting under physiological constraints. Concurrently, the rectifier circuit is designed using harmonic balance analysis in ADS, with various diode models evaluated for maximizing RF-to-DC conversion efficiency. The proposed system achieves a peak efficiency of 88.65%, with SAR values maintained well below regulatory limits across multiple implant positions. These findings underscore the potential of the proposed rectenna architecture to enable safe and efficient wireless powering of next-generation IMDs, thereby advancing the frontier of biomedical telemetry and implantable electronics.

articleTitle: Applications of Integrated Circuit Devices for improved Service Marketing Strategies
abstract: The contemporary research discovers the role of integrated circuit (IC) devices in improving the service delivery within the telecommunication industry to measure their impact on customer experience and network efficiency. The research focuses on the problem of optimizing technological infrastructure to meet the increasing demand for high-speed, reliable communication services. The objectives of the research are to understand the perceptions of telecommunication service providers about the contribution of IC devices to service performance and their effect on customer satisfaction. A qualitative research method was used, involving in-depth interviews with industry professionals and stakeholders from telecommunication service providers in northern India. The findings reveal a consensus on the importance of IC devices in driving network reliability, speed, and service innovation, while highlighting challenges in implementation and integration. These insights emphasize the strategic value of IC devices in shaping the future of telecommunication services, offering a competitive edge to service providers through technological excellence.

articleTitle: Lumbar Disc Herniation Detection and Classification in Sagittal, High-Resolution T2-Weighted MRI using Modified Attention U-NET
abstract: Lumbar Disc Herniation (LDH) is a prevalent spinal disorder causing severe pain and neurological complications, requiring timely and precise diagnosis. Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) provides detailed visualization of spinal abnormalities, yet manual analysis takes a lot of time and is subject to inter-observer variability. Existing deep learning approaches, such as U-Net, struggle with overfitting and unstable training, limiting their generalization. This study addresses these gaps by proposing a Modified Attention U-Net, integrating batch normalization (BN) after each convolutional layer to stabilize training and dropout (0.3) in the bottleneck layer to mitigate overfitting. Evaluated on T2-weighted sagittal MRI scans of 282 patients (1410 slices), the model achieves 87% classification accuracy, outperforming the baseline U-Net (80%). The validation accuracy curve demonstrates enhanced stability and robustness, unlike the fluctuating performance of the baseline U-Net. These advancements improve feature learning and model generalization, making the proposed method a promising automated tool for LDH detection.

articleTitle: Role of the Internet of Things and Wireless Sensor Networks in Automation of Wildlife Sanctuaries
abstract: Wildlife sanctuaries are vital ecosystems housing endangered and protected species, making it critical to preserve biodiversity and maintain ecological balance. While monitoring animals and habitat is challenging, including technological advancements such as IoT and Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) can significantly improve wildlife sanctuary operations. The Internet of Things offers a system of interconnected devices and sensors collecting and exchanging real-time data, including temperature, humidity, and animal activity. Automation is equally valuable- leveraging technology to manage resources, monitor animal movements, and track weather patterns. By implementing IoT and WSN technology, wildlife sanctuaries can benefit from improved insights into the conditions of the sanctuary and behavior of wildlife, ultimately promoting sanctuary preservation. The Internet of Things (IoT) along with automation is a great technological advancement that can bring about various benefits to wildlife sanctuaries. The monitoring of wildlife and their habitat is critical for sustaining and enhancing natural ecosystems. This article looks at the role of IoT and WSNs in automation for improvisation of wildlife sanctuaries.

articleTitle: A High-Performance Two-Stage OTA for Low Frequency Signal Amplification in Power Constrained Systems
abstract: This paper introduces a high-performance two-stage operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) designed to achieve superior stability and noise performance while operating under stringent power constraints. Existing OTA designs struggle with stability, power efficiency, and noise suppression trade-offs, making them less effective for precision analog applications. The proposed OTA addresses these limitations through an advanced transconductance-biasing approach and optimized compensation techniques to ensure a high phase margin, reduced distortion, and a robust gain-bandwidth product (GBW). Implemented in 90-nm CMOS technology with an 800mV supply voltage, the OTA is optimized for applications such as health monitoring, wearable devices, and low-power sensor networks, where energy efficiency and signal fidelity are critical. The design effectively tackles key challenges such as noise suppression, power efficiency, and precise low-frequency signal amplification. Simulation results obtained using Cadence Spectre demonstrate a common-mode gain of 89 dB, a GBW of 1.28 MHz, and a phase margin of 63°. Additionally, the OTA achieves a common-mode rejection ratio (CMRR) exceeding 100 dB and an input-referred noise of 17 pV/√Hz, with a power dissipation of just 1.9 μW and a Power Supply Rejection Ratio (PSRR) of 90 dB. These results underscore the OTA's ability to amplify very low-frequency signals with high precision, making it an ideal solution for power-constrained systems requiring reliable and accurate performance. Despite advancements in OTA architectures, prior research has highlighted significant challenges in achieving high gain and low noise while maintaining an optimal trade-off between bandwidth and stability. Here the proposed OTA presents a novel approach that balances stability, gain, bandwidth, and power efficiency.

articleTitle: Assessment of Indian Saffron (Crocus sativus L.) Quality Using Image Analysis and GC-MS-Based Aroma Profiling
abstract: Saffron, derived from Crocus sativus L., is a highly valued spice known for its color, flavor, aroma, and medicinal properties. Predominantly cultivated in Kashmir, India, its quality depends on crocin (color), picrocrocin (taste), and safranal (aroma). This study analyzed six saffron samples-two from Kashmir (Budgam, Kishtwar), two commercial (Mongra, Laccha), and two local (Local1, Local2)-using image analysis and GC-MS profiling. Parameters like red intensity, thread length, and gloss variance were assessed, alongside GC-MS aroma profiling. The Budgam sample had the highest quality score (0.789), while Laccha ranked lowest (0.077). A strong correlation (Spearman 0.942) was found between red intensity, safranal content, and quality. Image analysis and GC-MS showed a mean absolute error of 0.20 and RMSE of 0.23. The study highlights the effectiveness of combining image-based techniques with GC-MS for saffron quality assessment.

articleTitle: A Wearable EEG-Based Hybrid CNN-RNN Framework for Psychiatric Disorder Diagnosis: Leveraging XAI for Enhanced Clinical Insights
abstract: Mental health disorders like schizophrenia, anxiety, and depression are major causes of disability worldwide, yet diagnosis remains difficult due to the lack of objective biomarkers. This study introduces a hybrid CNN-RNN framework leveraging wearable EEG sensors and deep learning for more accurate diagnostics. CNNs extract spatial features, while RNNs model temporal patterns, improving performance over traditional and standalone deep learning models. Evaluated on public and custom datasets, the model achieves superior accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and ROC-AUC. Explainable AI techniques enhance interpretability, identifying clinically relevant EEG patterns. Cross-Dataset validation confirms robustness, though challenges like dataset size, real-time processing, and ethical concerns remain. This approach advances objective, data-driven mental health diagnostics, promoting more effective and accessible care.

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Network Modelling of Sub-Millimeter-Wave Silicon IMPATT Sources
abstract: This study investigates artificial neural networks (ANNs) for predicting the millimeter-wave (mm-wave) and sub-millimeter-wave (sub-mm-wave) characteristics of Double-Drift Region (DDR) Si IMPATT diodes. The ANN models predict key parameters, including DC, large-signal (L-S) performance, and avalanche noise across 94–500 GHz. Training data from self-consistent quantum drift-diffusion (SCQDD) simulations enable the models to capture structural, doping, and biasing effects accurately. The ANN approach significantly reduces computational time, predicting device characteristics in just 4.4% to 15% of the time required for SCQDD simulations while maintaining high accuracy. The mean square error (MSE) for breakdown voltage and power output remains in the order of 10⁻<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> Unit<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, demonstrating strong predictive performance. Validation against experimental data confirms excellent agreement in power output, efficiency, and noise characteristics. These results highlight the potential of machine learning to replace conventional time-intensive simulations, offering a powerful tool for the rapid design and optimization of high-frequency semiconductor devices.
